data/inner-workings/variables/coarse-san.title: Coarse sand_DK (200–2000 µm), % of the whole soil
data/inner-workings/variables/coarse-san.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScaleratioValue typefloatReference systemunit: % of the dry mass of the whole soil, organic matter included (QUDT PERCENT)Leafcoarse-sand-content
_DK — Danish size classes. The Danish texture classes put the limits at 2, 20, 200 and 2000 µm. Clay (< 2 µm) is the international limit, but Danish silt (2–20 µm), fine sand (20–200 µm) and coarse sand (200–2000 µm) are not the silt and sand of USDA/FAO (2–50 µm; 50–2000 µm) or ISO 14688 (2–63 µm; 63–2000 µm). The names are kept, with the postfix _DK, so a reader comparing with international data sees at once that the classes differ.
Coarse sand on the whole-soil basis.
Relations

convertible to: coarse-sand-mass-fraction, rule: x · 100 / (100 − humus − CaCO3), requires: humus-mass-fraction; carbonate-mass-fraction
aggregates of: medium-sand-mass-fraction-whole-soil; coarse-sand-500-2000-mass-fraction-whole-soil, rule: sum

data/inner-workings/variables/silt-mass-.title: Silt_DK (2–20 µm), % of the whole soil
data/inner-workings/variables/silt-mass-.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScaleratioValue typefloatReference systemunit: % of the dry mass of the whole soil, organic matter included (QUDT PERCENT)Leafsilt-content
_DK — Danish size classes. The Danish texture classes put the limits at 2, 20, 200 and 2000 µm. Clay (< 2 µm) is the international limit, but Danish silt (2–20 µm), fine sand (20–200 µm) and coarse sand (200–2000 µm) are not the silt and sand of USDA/FAO (2–50 µm; 50–2000 µm) or ISO 14688 (2–63 µm; 63–2000 µm). The names are kept, with the postfix _DK, so a reader comparing with international data sees at once that the classes differ.
Silt on the whole-soil basis.

data/inner-workings/variables/silt-mass-.title: Silt_DK (2–20 µm)
data/inner-workings/variables/silt-mass-.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScaleratioValue typefloatReference systemunit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)Leafsilt-content
_DK — Danish size classes. The Danish texture classes put the limits at 2, 20, 200 and 2000 µm. Clay (< 2 µm) is the international limit, but Danish silt (2–20 µm), fine sand (20–200 µm) and coarse sand (200–2000 µm) are not the silt and sand of USDA/FAO (2–50 µm; 50–2000 µm) or ISO 14688 (2–63 µm; 63–2000 µm). The names are kept, with the postfix _DK, so a reader comparing with international data sees at once that the classes differ.
Texture fractions are a share of the mineral fraction (the four fractions sum to 100 %), not of the whole soil as SOC and carbonate are. Tekstur2024 maps them as if organic matter had been removed before analysis (SOM_removal = 1 in the model); the 1970s survey did not remove it, which gives less clay and more silt. That method is part of the variable.
Realised by: Tekstur2024 v1.1 (4 depths × mean, sd, q05, q95), Tekstur2014 (without the organic-matter correction — strictly another variable).
Relations (pilot 3)

convertible from silt-mass-fraction-whole-soil (whole-soil basis): x · 100 / (100 − humus − CaCO3). The national samples, Kvadratnettet and the 2008 grid report this variable; Tekstur2024 reports this one.

data/inner-workings/variables/soc-mass-f.title: SOC mass fraction, classes
data/inner-workings/variables/soc-mass-f.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScaleordinalValue typeintegerReference systemcode-list: 4 classes; the value is the class’s upper limit in % (3, 6, 12, 60)Leafsoil-organic-carbon
The SOC mass fraction in four classes; the cell value is the upper limit of the class.
The limits carry meaning: 6 % is the limit for carbon-rich lowland soils in Tørv2022 and, from 2024, for soil type JB11 (before: 5.87 %); 12 % is the usual limit for organic soils. Accuracy of the classes (positive predictive value, 0–30 cm, Kulstof2022): ≤ 6 %: 99 %, 6–12 %: 24 %, > 12 %: 68 % (Møller et al. 2024a, table 7) — the middle class is hard to get right.

data/inner-workings/variables/soc-mass-f.title: SOC mass fraction
data/inner-workings/variables/soc-mass-f.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScaleratioValue typefloatReference systemunit: % of the dry mass of the fine earth (< 2 mm) (QUDT PERCENT)Leafsoil-organic-carbon
Soil organic carbon as a share of the soil’s dry mass, in % (1 % = 10 g/kg). In I-ADOPT terms: property mass fraction, object of interest organic carbon, matrix soil (fine earth, sieved < 2 mm), constraint depth interval (a layer dimension) and analytical method.
Leaf: Soil organic carbon.
Realised by: Kulstofkort i 10 m, v1.1 (16 layers: 4 depths × mean, sd, q05, q95), Tørv2022, Tekstur2014, and the point datasets listed on the leaf.
Why the method is a constraint. The Danish samples behind the maps were analysed with comparable methods, so they share one variable. A source analysed differently (loss on ignition converted to carbon, for instance) would be a different variable, related by a conversion that is itself uncertain: the old JB11 limit of 5.87 % SOC came from assuming organic matter is 58.7 % carbon, which Møller et al. (2024a) call more uncertain than the difference it makes.

data/inner-workings/variables/soc-stock.title: SOC stock
data/inner-workings/variables/soc-stock.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScaleratioValue typefloatReference systemunit: Mg C per ha to a stated depth (QUDT TONNE-PER-HA)Leafsoil-organic-carbon
The mass of organic carbon per area down to a stated depth, in Mg C/ha. It is computed from the mass fraction, the bulk density and the stone content of each layer, so a map of the mass fraction cannot be compared with a stock map without those. Kept here to show why the leaf needs variables: both answer “how much carbon?”, in different quantities.

data/inner-workings/variables/soil-type-.title: Danish soil type (JB number)
data/inner-workings/variables/soil-type-.content:
Aboutworld — a property of the thing in the worldScalenominalValue typeintegerReference systemcode-list: JB classes; the scheme is part of the reference (jb-1992, jb-2024, jb-2024-jb4-split, lbst-nitrogen-norm)Leafsoil-type-jb
The Danish soil-type classification (jordbundstype, JB1–JB12) from texture, organic carbon and carbonate in the topsoil, used in regulation (farms’ nitrogen quotas).
It is the clearest case in the pilot of why class definitions must be versioned and attributed:



































SchemeWhoJB11JB4jb-1992the national soil classificationhumus > 10 % (SOC > 5.87 %)JB4jb-2024AU Agroecology, Møller et al. 2024aSOC > 6 %JB4jb-2024-jb4-splitAU Agroecology, Greve 2024SOC > 6 %JB41 (sandy/peaty subsoil), JB42 (clayey subsoil)lbst-nitrogen-normLandbrugsstyrelsenSOC > 6 %JB41 → JB4, JB42 → JB6
The last row is the academic/administrative split in one line: the authority recodes JB42 as JB6 for its nitrogen rules, while the scientists refuse to, “because the JB classification is by definition a topsoil classification and cannot include the subsoil” (Greve 2024, translated). Both are legitimate; a catalogue that stores only “JB6” loses which one it is.
Realised by: JB2024; earlier soil types in the live catalogue: Jordbundstyper (sgis-000976, scheme jb-1992).
Schemes (notes)
The code list is part of the reference, and each edition is a note of its own: ddj-farvekode, jb-1992, jb-2024, jb-2024-jb4-split, lbst-nitrogen-norm.

data/inner-workings/versions/ais-vessel-.title: AIS vessel positions: daily files
data/inner-workings/versions/ais-vessel-.content:
The columns as they are named in the demo file. Names, type, size, draught, destination and ETA are typed in by the crew and can be wrong. The source states neither units nor time zone.

















































































































ColumnMeaningtimetime of the report from the base station. The source does not state the time zonemobile_typekind of sender: Class A, Class B, SAR Airborne, Search and Rescue TranspondermmsiMMSI number of the sendernavigational_statusnavigational status from the AIS message, set by the crewrate_of_turnrate of turn from the AIS messagespeed_over_groundspeed over ground from the AIS message (knots in the AIS standard; the source does not state the unit)course_over_groundcourse over ground from the AIS message, degreesheadingheading from the AIS message, degrees; values above 359 occur and are not valid headingsimoIMO number of the vessel; empty where the source says Unknowncallsigncallsign of the vesselnamename of the vessel, as sentship_typeAIS ship type, as sentcargo_typecargo category from the AIS messagewidthwidth of the vessel (metres in the AIS standard)lengthlength of the vessel (metres in the AIS standard)position_devicetype of positioning devicedraughtdraught, as entered by the crew (metres in the AIS standard)destinationdestination, free text entered by the crewetaestimated time of arrival, as entered by the crewdata_sourcedata source type; AIS in all rowssize_alength from GPS to the bowsize_blength from GPS to the sternsize_clength from GPS to starboard sidesize_dlength from GPS to port sidelatitudelatitude; empty where the source has an impossible valuelongitudelongitude; empty where the source has an impossible value
The demo day has 9,248,732 positions from 2,716 senders (the source file: 15,058,275 rows, of which 936,518 from base stations; aids to navigation and exact duplicates are also left out), joined into 3,948 lines of 2,607 vessels. Vessels send at different rates: counting points is not counting traffic.
The area covered changes from day to day (on 15 July 2026 from 3° W to 20° E, on most days 5–16° E), so cut to a fixed area before comparing days.

Abstract
Kortlaget indeholder arealer med restriktioner for arealanvendelse som følge af forbud mod sprøjtning og / eller gødskning. Restriktionerne følger primært af aftaler med lodsejere, som vandselskaberne har indgået ifm. grundvandsbeskyttelse.
Beskrivelse hentet d. 15/07/2024 fra miljoegis.mim.dk/cbkort

Attribution

Indeholder data fra Styrelsen for Grøn Arealomlægning og Vandmiljø, Arealer med pesticid- og gødningsfri drift, 2024, WMS-tjeneste

The line names the WMS-tjeneste you use; for a downloaded file write hentet ‹date› (the date you downloaded it) instead. In QGIS, right-click it in the SemanticGIS panel and choose Copy attribution.



Affiliation history

Datasets change hands when ministries are reorganised, and reports, maps and older metadata keep the name of the agency of their time. Every agency this dataset has been filed under in SemanticGIS is kept here; the dates are when SemanticGIS recorded it, not when the responsibility moved.

Styrelsen for Grøn Arealomlægning og Vandmiljø (current): recorded 2026-11-11, in Danmarks Miljøportal (dataset owner). The agency was created in September 2024 under the new Ministeriet for Grøn Trepart (the green tripartite agreement); most of Landbrugsstyrelsen’s staff and parts of Miljøstyrelsen moved to it (Altinget, 25 September 2024).
Landbrugsstyrelsen: recorded 2026-04-18 to 2026-11-11, in the geodata-info.dk metadata.

Two time axes, in practice
Every version of a polling district carries valid time (virkningstid: when it holds in the world) and registration time (registreringstid: when the register recorded it), each with the actor responsible, plus the business event (forretningshændelse) and process that caused the change. Datafordeler’s GraphQL API answers the bitemporal question directly: what did the register, as it stood at R, say was valid at V?
One rural district, Ejer Bavnehøj (700784, Skanderborg), asked at five valid times (rows) as the register stood at five registration times (columns). Each cell: the version returned, as valid from / registered.





















































valid at ↓ / as registered at →2019-06-012023-06-012024-06-012025-06-012026-11-192019-01-01v2018-03-05 / r2018-03-05v2018-03-05 / r2022-11-30v2018-03-05 / r2022-11-30v2018-03-05 / r2022-11-30v2018-03-05 / r2022-11-302023-01-01v2018-03-05 / r2018-03-05v2022-11-29 / r2023-03-20v2022-11-29 / r2023-03-20v2022-11-29 / r2023-03-20v2022-11-29 / r2023-03-202024-01-01v2018-03-05 / r2018-03-05v2023-03-19 / r2023-03-20v2023-03-19 / r2023-03-20v2023-03-19 / r2024-10-03v2023-03-19 / r2024-10-032025-06-01v2018-03-05 / r2018-03-05v2023-03-19 / r2023-03-20v2023-03-19 / r2023-03-20v2024-10-02 / r2024-10-03v2024-10-02 / r2026-07-012026-11-19v2018-03-05 / r2018-03-05v2023-03-19 / r2023-03-20v2023-03-19 / r2023-03-20v2024-10-02 / r2024-10-03v2026-07-01 / r2026-07-01
Read along a row: the same moment in the world, as the register knew it at different times. In the 2024-01-01 row the answer changes between mid-2024 and mid-2025 — a correction registered on 2024-10-03 closed the version’s validity retroactively. The 2026-07-01 column change is a system migration (SystemMigreringDagi3, event Fejlrettelse) that re-registered 413 districts at once. Read down the first column: as the register stood in 2019, nothing after 2018 existed — obviously, but it is what makes an analysis on an old extract reproducible.
For this district every version has the same area (60.3109 km²); only the number of vertices changes (1 197 → 1 441 → 1 437) — map-matching to GeoDanmark (FOTAjourføring) and corrections, not redistricting. Most versions are not changes in the world. The event field is what tells the two apart.
A real redistricting: Roskilde, 21 August 2026
The municipality of Roskilde had 18 polling districts on 1 January 2026 and has 15 now (valid time 2026-11-19, registered now):



































































































































id2026-01-012026-11-1970279406 Himmelev06 Himmelevunchanged70432011 Gundsølille11 Gundsølilleunchanged70435003 Sankt Jørgen—ended 2026-08-2170435813 Jyllinge—ended 2026-08-2170437805 Østervang05 Østervangunchanged70439608 Vindinge08 Vindingeunchanged70440221 Trekroner21 Trekronerunchanged70590007 Svogerslev07 Svogerslevunchanged70728401 Roskilde Bymidte—ended 2026-08-2170731416 Gadstrup16 Gadstrupunchanged70732617 Viby17 Vibyunchanged70733218 Snoldelev18 Snoldelevunchanged70880602 Klostermarken02 Klostermarkenunchanged71040415 Baunehøj—ended 2026-08-2171047604 Hedegårdene04 Hedegårdeneunchanged71168009 Vor Frue09 Vor Frueunchanged71168614 Gundsømagle14 Gundsømagleunchanged71171010 Tjørnegård—ended 2026-08-21749449—22 Roskilde Kongrescenternew 2026-08-21749450—13 Jyllingenew 2026-08-21
Valid from 2026-08-21 11:02 and 11:08, registered two minutes later each, by Kommunen (event KommunalAjourføring). Note Jyllinge: number 13 and the same name before and after, but a new identifier (704358 → 749450) — the register treats it as a new district. A student who joins election results across years by name and number would join two different areas; one who joins by id_lokalId would see a break where the name suggests continuity. The model records identity explicitly (identity: id_lokalId) so that this is visible.
What is backdated, and what is not
In the current versions, registration follows valid time within a day (all 1 305: 0–0.7 days). DAGI’s valid time is in practice the time of the edit, not of the decision; backdating appears only through corrections that close earlier versions (the 2024-10-03 case). Registers where facts are routinely backdated — dwellings in BBR, ownership in the land register — will show large gaps; DAGI is the mild case.
Representations: defined, not produced
The data model defines 1:250 000, 1:500 000 and 1:2 000 000 representations of the polling districts (there is no 1:50 000). Since the move to DAGI’s new administration system in July 2026 they are not produced: “Entiteter med underscore _250000, _500000 og _20000000 kan ikke anvendes, da der i DAGIs nye forvaltningssystem ikke findes et system, der generaliserer data” (KDS, Fildownload (DAGI)). On 2026-11-19 the WFS layers and the V3 and V4 file downloads for those scales are empty (0 rows); the Dataforsyningen services that used to deliver them answer 404. The model therefore distinguishes a representation that is defined from one that is delivered, with a date — and here the reason is a change of system, not a gap in our query.
Two kinds of version: domain model and service
DAGI has domain models that change rarely and with large consequences, and service versions that change how the data are delivered. Source: DAGI Versionshistorik in Grunddatamodel, domænemodeller and KDS’s Versioner af tjenester.






























Domain modelDateChange1.0.0delivered 2015-02-13, approved 2015-03-17first model1.0.12016-02-09—1.0.22024-05-27CRS and whether Z is real stated on the geometry (rule 5.11)2.0.0approved 2024-12-12 (the object type catalogue says 2024-10-21)Storkreds and Valglandsdel added; 1:250 000, 1:500 000, 1:2 000 000 as separate classes; Menighedsrådsafstemningsområde removed; general attributes removed; relations simplified






























Service (2026-11-19)VersionsDomain model deliveredFile download4 (newest), 3, 14 and 3: model 2.0.0, identical columns — the documented difference is that “fra Version 4 bliver den specifikke geometritype angivet”; 1: frozen, “data opdateres ikke”GraphQLv2model 2.0.0, bitemporalEntity-based WFS / WMS1.0.0 (dagi_v001)model 2.0.0, current state onlyOld GeoServer WFS DAGIM/DAGI_*MULTIGEOM*1.0.0model 1.x, frozen; phased out 2027-01-15
Model 2.0.0 went into production with the new administration system (DAGI3) on 2026-07-02; the migration shows in the register as SystemMigreringDagi3 on 2026-07-01. The generalised classes exist in model 2.0.0 but are not produced, because the new system has no generalisation. The old model-1 services still hold the last generalised polling districts (1 315, from the 2025 local elections) and the church-council polling districts (a class removed in 2.0.0). Both are snapshotted before the services disappear: afstemningsomraade_sgis-000940/2026-03-27/ and menighedsraadsafstemningsomraade_sgis-002183/2026-04-01/. Model 1’s history service gives registration time but no virkningTil — a register history, not a full bitemporal table: one more thing that changed between the models.
None of them is a version in the model’s sense (a release of the dataset): the register has no releases. They belong on the distribution (download version), on the documentation (model version) and in the lineage of the registrations (system migration).
The whole history in one file
Datafordeler’s file download DAGI_V4_Afstemningsomraade_TotalDownload_gpkg_Bitemporal is the register’s complete bitemporal table as a GeoPackage: 29 863 rows for 1 548 districts (1 305 current, 243 ended), 3D multipolygons in EPSG:25832, with the same fields as the services. Each change adds two rows — one that ends the old registration, one that records the old version with its closed validity — so Ejer Bavnehøj has nine rows, matching the GraphQL grid above exactly. The file is a snapshot without saying so: its newest registration is 2026-10-09 10:30, and it was written on 2026-10-11, although the download fetched on 2026-11-19 is numbered 264 and the file inside 230. The registration cutoff, not the download date, is the snapshot date.
Two filters in QGIS answer the bitemporal question without any API:

















QuestionFilter on the layerThe districts valid on date D, as known now"registreringtil" IS NULL AND "virkningfra" <= 'D' AND ("virkningtil" IS NULL OR "virkningtil" > 'D')The districts valid on D, as the register stood on R"registreringfra" <= 'R' AND ("registreringtil" IS NULL OR "registreringtil" > 'R') AND "virkningfra" <= 'D' AND ("virkningtil" IS NULL OR "virkningtil" > 'D')
Polling districts on election days, as known now:








































ElectionDateDistrictsGeneral election2019-06-051 384Local elections2021-11-161 384General election2022-11-011 347European Parliament2024-06-091 298Local elections2025-11-181 315—2026-11-191 305
Districts are created and ended in bursts before elections (May 2022: 10 created, 37 ended; February–March 2024: 23 created, 56 ended; October 2024; August 2026). Of 11 338 versions opened since 2018, 96.5 % were registered within a day of taking effect; 16 more than 30 days later (the longest 393 days, corrections in 2024). Changes from an amended regulation (ændretBekendtgørelse) were registered a median 17.5 days before they took effect — forward-dated, the mirror image of backdating: the register knew of the change before it was true.
Snapshot
A snapshot of the register fixes registration time: the register as it stood at its last registration. On the RUC data share: datasets/afstemningsomraade_sgis-000940/2026-10-09/ — the full bitemporal history as GeoParquet (42 MB against 673 MB as GeoPackage; geometry 2D because every Z was 0, time fields typed as UTC timestamps, sorted by id and time), with a README holding the two QGIS filters and a code list of the business events. Dated by the registration cutoff (2026-10-09 10:30), not by the download (2026-11-19). From now on vector snapshots on the share are GeoParquet by default.

data/inner-workings/versions/geoilum-geo.title: GeoILUM geotopes, Region Zealand — v0.1
data/inner-workings/versions/geoilum-geo.content:
Version 0.1 of GeoILUM geotopes, Region Zealand: 377 687 geotopes in 16 categories, described in Christensen, Holmes & Nielsen (2026).
Variables (the schema)
The variables this version realises. Depth, statistic and support are not part of a variable; they are the layer’s place in the version’s grid (next section), so SOC_q95_030_060_cm is soc-mass-fraction at 30–60 cm, 95 % quantile.





















































































































VariableAboutScaleReference systemLeafgeotope-idrecordnominalidentifier-scheme: integer, unique within one version of the geotope map; not persistent across versions— (does not realise a leaf)geotope-extentworldnoneCRS: EPSG:25832 (ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N), polygonsgeotopegeotope-categoryworldnominalcode-list: scheme geoilum-sj-k16: categories 1–16 of one model rungeotopeterrain-slopeworldratiounit: % (rise over run × 100)surface-form (planned)topographic-position-indexworldintervalunit: dimensionless, −1 (valley) … 1 (ridge), 250 × 250 m neighbourhoodsurface-form (planned)topographic-wetness-indexworldintervalunit: dimensionless, ln(a / tan β)surface-form (planned)solar-radiation-daily-meanworldratiounit: Wh/m² per day, clear sky, with terrain shadingsurface-form (planned)groundwater-depth (summer)worldintervalunit and vertical datum: cm below the terrain surface, positive downward; negative = water above the surfacegroundwater (planned)groundwater-depth (winter)worldintervalunit and vertical datum: cm below the terrain surface, positive downward; negative = water above the surfacegroundwater (planned)clay-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)clay-content (planned)silt-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)silt-content (planned)fine-sand-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)fine-sand-content (planned)coarse-sand-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)coarse-sand-content (planned)carbonate-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the dry mass of the fine earth (< 2 mm) (QUDT PERCENT)carbonate-content (planned)soc-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the dry mass of the fine earth (< 2 mm) (QUDT PERCENT)soil-organic-carbon
Layers (the realisations)
Each attribute realises a variable with a different support than its source: the mean over a geotope’s 10 m cells, not a value per cell. Same variable, new statistic, new support — which is why support sits on the layer.

The attribute table documents itself: every column carries a JSON comment (project, role, description, version) — a good pattern, and one the catalogue could read directly. Two slips in it: the winter groundwater column is described as sommer, and the SOC column has no comment.
Lineage

























InputRoleNoteRUC topsoil 2024differentiating variablesfrom Tekstur2024 (and SOC from Kulstofkort?), processed at RUCDanish terrain model, 0.4 m (2023)differentiating variablesslope, TPI, wetness, solar radiation; to match in the catalogueHIP near-surface groundwater (Henriksen et al.)differentiating variablessummer and winter depth; to match in the catalogue
So SOC reaches the geotopes in three steps: Kulstofkort/Tekstur2024 (AU) → RUC topsoil 2024 (gap-filled, filtered) → mean per geotope. Each step is a node with its own version and its own changes to the values; a student following SOC from a sample in the 1970s to a geotope attribute can see all of them.

Each distribution says what it delivers and its status, and maps its own file paths (asset_map, rasters) or column names (column_map, vector) to the version’s layers and variables — the same rule as for the DAGI services in pilot 2. data/inner-workings/versions/glm-7-samme.content:
Version 2025 of GLM 7 samme afgrødekategori i 3 år.
SGIS reference: sgis-001864
Abstract
Kortlaget viser de arealer, der har været indberettet til SGAV med samme afgrødekategori i 2022, 2023 og 2024. Data viser som hovedregel afgrødekategorien for 2024. Kortlaget bruges til at validere, om den afgrødekategori, der indberettes i 2025, er tilladt i forhold til GLM7, delkrav 2, som er et krav om at man højest må have samme afgrødekategori tre år i træk på samme omdriftsareal. Der er dog en undtagelse for kravet for majs med græsudlæg og tidligt høstede spisekartofler med efterafgrøde. Undtagelsen er afspejlet i data.

data/inner-workings/versions/godkendt-ti.content:
Version 2017 of Godkendt til øko biavl.
SGIS reference: sgis-001450
Abstract
Kortet viser områder, der kunne godkendes til økologisk biavl i 2017. Økologiske bigårde skal placeres, så bierne har adgang til at trække på 95% godkendte nektar- og pollenkilder inden for en radius af bigården på 3 km. Nektar- og pollenkilder betragtes som godkendte, hvis de stammer fra økologiske arealer, miljøvenligt drevne arealer eller naturarealer.

data/inner-workings/versions/helcom-ais-.content:
2017 and 2018 are missing at the source.
2021 and 2022 are in EPSG:3857, the other years in EPSG:3035. Counts per cell cannot be compared between the two.
2010: the band all is 1.7 % lower than the sum of the types; in every other year they agree.
Fishing rises from 0.4 million cell crossings (2006) to about 3 million (2014). More vessels had to carry AIS in the period, so the rise is not only traffic.

data/inner-workings/versions/kulstofkort.title: Kulstofkort i 10 m, version 1.1 (2024-07-04)
data/inner-workings/versions/kulstofkort.content:
Version 1.1 of Kulstofkort i 10 m opløsning, described in Møller, Greve & Beucher (2024a).
Variables (the schema)
The variables this version realises. Depth, statistic and support are not part of a variable; they are the layer’s place in the version’s grid (next section), so SOC_q95_030_060_cm is soc-mass-fraction at 30–60 cm, 95 % quantile.

































VariableAboutScaleReference systemLeafsoc-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the dry mass of the fine earth (< 2 mm) (QUDT PERCENT)soil-organic-carbonsoc-mass-fraction-classworldordinalcode-list: 4 classes; the value is the class’s upper limit in % (3, 6, 12, 60)soil-organic-carbonsoc-source-maprecordnominalcode-list: 1 = Tørv2022, 2 = Tekstur2024— (does not realise a leaf)
Layers (the realisations)
Each layer realises one variable at one depth with one statistic, and comes from one of the two named maps of the report.

The topsoil is different from the deeper layers, and the model has to say so. Its mean and classes are Kulstof2022: values from Tørv2022 in historic peat areas and wherever SOC > 6 %, from Tekstur2024 elsewhere. The combination layer records which was used in each cell, and the uncertainty layers were cut to the Tekstur2024 part, because Tørv2022 has its own uncertainty maps.
Time
The samples span 1970–2022: the soil classification survey (1970s), the forest surveys (1979–82, 1990–91), the profile database (1980–2021), SINKS (2009–10), SEGES’s field samples and Tørv2022’s newest samples (2022). Because SOC changes over decades, older samples were down-weighted by 0.99 per year of age. The authors therefore name SOC maps after the year of the latest samples (Kulstof2022, Tørv2022) but texture maps after the year of publication (Tekstur2024), since texture hardly changes. The same team uses the two time axes of the model — when observed, when issued — in its own naming.

data/inner-workings/versions/kvaelstofre.content:
Version 2020 of Kvælstofretention.
SGIS reference: sgis-001541
Abstract
Kortet viser hvor stor en procentdel af kvælstof, der omsættes eller tilbageholdes i undergrunden eller overfladevandet, fra kvælstof udvaskes fra rodzonen til det når frem til kysten. Kvælstofretentionen er beregnet med den Nationale Kvælstofmodel som en gennemsnitlig retention for perioden 1990-2010. Den Nationale Kvælstofmodel version 2020 er beskrevet i: National kvælstofmodel - version 2020, GEUS specialrapport. Metode rapport: ISBN 978-87-7871-551-7 Bilag: ISBN 978-87-7871-552-4. Begge rapporter kan downloades fra www.geus.dk
Kortet er udviklet i perioden medio 2013 til primo 2015 af GEUS og Aarhus Universitet (DCE og DCA). Kortet er revideret august 2015. Forklaring til indhold af kolonner: ID: Unikt ID15 opland nummer RedTot: Samlede retention af kvælstof i procent fra det udvaskes fra rodzonen indenfor et ID15 opland til det når et kystafsnit RedSurf: Samlede retention af kvælstof i procent fra det strømmer til overfladevandet indenfor ID15 oplandet og til det når et kystafsnit RedGW: Reduktion af kvælstof i undergrunden i procent fra det udvaskes indenfor et ID15 opland til det når frem til overfladevandssystemet MinRedTot: Minimale samlet retention i procent fra rodzonen til kyst (RedTot - UncRedTot) MaxRedTot: Maksimale samlet retention i procent fra rodzonen til kyst (RedTot + UncRedTot) UncRedTot: Usikkerhedsestimat på samlet reduktionsprocent angivet i procentpoint BiasReg: Bias Region InModel: 1: ID15 opland i målt opland; 0: ID15 opland i umålt opland; -1: ID15 opland ligger udenfor modelområde, samlet retention er estimeret som middel af samlet retention for øvrige umålte oplande. Kilde: Geus. 15-12-2020

data/inner-workings/versions/np3b2020-fi.title: NP3b2020 Fiskeriintensitet 2013
data/inner-workings/versions/np3b2020-fi.content:
Version 2013 of NP3b2020 Fiskeriintensitet.
SGIS reference: sgis-000804
Abstract
Temaet viser fiskeriintensiteten med bundslæbende redskaber i kvadrater på 100x100m fra danske fartøjer. Intensiteten fortæller hvor mange gange havbunden i de enkelte kvadrater er blevet påvirket af fiskeredskaber i 2013. For værdier under 1 kan intensiteten tolkes som den andel af kvadratet, der er blevet påvirket i perioden. Kortet er udarbejdet vha. forskellige typer positionsdata (VMS, AIS, Black Box) med varierende præcision og registreringseffektivitet. Intensiteten er beregnet som “swept area ratio” (SAR) ved at dele periodens samlede redskabspåvirkning i hvert kvadrat (fodaftrykket målt i m2) med arealet af kvadratet (10.000 m2).
Filnavn: np3basis2020_sar_2013

SGIS reference: sgis-001645
Abstract
Kortet viser stabile områder, der kunne godkendes til økologisk biavl i alle 3 år 2016-18. Økologiske bigårde skal placeres, så bierne har adgang til at trække på 95 % godkendte nektar- og pollenkilder inden for en radius af
bigården på 3 km. Nektar- og pollenkilder betragtes som godkendte, hvis de stammer fra økologiske arealer, miljøvenligt drevne arealer eller
naturarealer.

SGIS reference: sgis-001392
Abstract
Datasættene/kortene indeholder information om den årlige mængde af kvælstof (gennemsnit over 3 år), som deponeres på planter, jord og vand fra luften. Depositionen er stedfæstet i et grid, hvor vægten af den samlede årlige deposition er beregnet for hvert kvadrat i griddet. Datasættene er resultat af modelberegninger med DEHM modellen udført af DCE, Aarhus Universitet ifm. delprogram for luft under NOVANA.

data/inner-workings/versions/sommer-orto.title: Sommer ortofoto 1999
data/inner-workings/versions/sommer-orto.content:
Version 1999 of Sommer ortofoto.
SGIS reference: sgis-001929
Abstract
DDO® er fotograferet efter løvspring, så både træer, buske og græs fremtræder i klare grønne farver, og så afgrøderne på markerne de fleste steder er i vækst. DDO® er derfor ideelt som illustrationskort, fordi det giver et tydeligt billede af landskab og byrum i klare farver. DDO® giver både overblik og detailinformation. Den høje opløsning giver mulighed for at identificere selv små detaljer, når man zoomer tæt ind på et sted, og samtidig skabe et hurtigt overblik. DDO® giver overblik over vegetationen samt mulighed for at identificere forekomst og fordeling af forskellige vegetationsarter. DDO® kan leveres i en traditionel farveudgave (RGB) og/eller i en farveinfrarød udgave (CIR), og CIR-udgaven er særligt velegnet som grundlag for klassifikation af fordelingen mellem befæstede og ubefæstede arealer. Årgang: 1999. Fotoperiode: 18.05 – 29.07. Fotogrundlag: 1:25000. Opløsning: 40 cm. Kilde: hxgncontent.com/products/regional-programs/denmark/dk Vær opmærksom på at der særlige licensbetingelser for dette datasæt: miljoeportal.dk/dataansvar/saerlige-vilkaar-for-brug-af-kort-fra-danmarks-arealinformation/

data/inner-workings/versions/sommer-orto.title: Sommer ortofoto 2002
data/inner-workings/versions/sommer-orto.content:
Version 2002 of Sommer ortofoto.
SGIS reference: sgis-001930
Abstract
DDO® er fotograferet efter løvspring, så både træer, buske og græs fremtræder i klare grønne farver, og så afgrøderne på markerne de fleste steder er i vækst. DDO® er derfor ideelt som illustrationskort, fordi det giver et tydeligt billede af landskab og byrum i klare farver. DDO® giver både overblik og detailinformation. Den høje opløsning giver mulighed for at identificere selv små detaljer, når man zoomer tæt ind på et sted, og samtidig skabe et hurtigt overblik. DDO® giver overblik over vegetationen samt mulighed for at identificere forekomst og fordeling af forskellige vegetationsarter. DDO® kan leveres i en traditionel farveudgave (RGB) og/eller i en farveinfrarød udgave (CIR), og CIR-udgaven er særligt velegnet som grundlag for klassifikation af fordelingen mellem befæstede og ubefæstede arealer. Årgang: 2002. Fotoperiode: 18.05 – 19.08. Fotogrundlag: 1:25000. Opløsning: 40 cm. data/inner-workings/versions/tekstur2024.title: Tekstur2024 v1.1 — maps of soil texture (2024-07-04)
data/inner-workings/versions/tekstur2024.content:
Version 1.1 of Tekstur2024: 80 layers, 4 depths × 5 variables × 4 statistics, 38.6 GB unpacked. Same model run, grid and date as Kulstofkort v1.1, which holds the SOC layers.
Variables (the schema)
The variables this version realises. Depth, statistic and support are not part of a variable; they are the layer’s place in the version’s grid (next section), so SOC_q95_030_060_cm is soc-mass-fraction at 30–60 cm, 95 % quantile.















































VariableAboutScaleReference systemLeafclay-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)clay-content (planned)silt-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)silt-content (planned)fine-sand-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)fine-sand-content (planned)coarse-sand-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the mineral fraction of the fine earth (< 2 mm); the four fractions sum to 100 (QUDT PERCENT)coarse-sand-content (planned)carbonate-mass-fractionworldratiounit: % of the dry mass of the fine earth (< 2 mm) (QUDT PERCENT)carbonate-content (planned)
Layers (the realisations)
























































































































































Depth (cm)VariableStatisticsFilesSize0-30clay-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Clay_<stat>_000_030_cm1.9 GB0-30silt-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Silt_<stat>_000_030_cm1.8 GB0-30fine-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Fine_sand_<stat>_000_030_cm2.6 GB0-30coarse-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Coarse_sand_<stat>_000_030_cm2.4 GB0-30carbonate-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95CaCO3_<stat>_000_030_cm0.5 GB30-60clay-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Clay_<stat>_030_060_cm1.9 GB30-60silt-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Silt_<stat>_030_060_cm1.8 GB30-60fine-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Fine_sand_<stat>_030_060_cm2.6 GB30-60coarse-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Coarse_sand_<stat>_030_060_cm2.4 GB30-60carbonate-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95CaCO3_<stat>_030_060_cm0.6 GB60-100clay-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Clay_<stat>_060_100_cm2.0 GB60-100silt-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Silt_<stat>_060_100_cm1.8 GB60-100fine-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Fine_sand_<stat>_060_100_cm2.7 GB60-100coarse-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Coarse_sand_<stat>_060_100_cm2.3 GB60-100carbonate-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95CaCO3_<stat>_060_100_cm0.9 GB100-200clay-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Clay_<stat>_100_200_cm2.1 GB100-200silt-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Silt_<stat>_100_200_cm1.9 GB100-200fine-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Fine_sand_<stat>_100_200_cm2.7 GB100-200coarse-sand-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95Coarse_sand_<stat>_100_200_cm2.3 GB100-200carbonate-mass-fractionmean, sd, q05, q95CaCO3_<stat>_100_200_cm1.3 GB
Quality
Accuracy falls steeply with depth, because there are few deep samples: clay has R²w 0.65 in the topsoil and 0.03 at 100–200 cm (independent test set; Møller et al. 2024a, table 3). The deep texture layers are best read through their q05–q95 range. Coarse sand: R²w 0.72 / RMSEw 9.7 % in the topsoil.
Distributions
Each distribution says what it delivers and its status, and maps its own file paths (asset_map, rasters) or column names (column_map, vector) to the version’s layers and variables — the same rule as for the DAGI services in pilot 2. Generated from the files on the RUC data share.


























IdProtocolDeliversStatusMap to layers/variablesau-hub-downloadfile download (ArcGIS Hub)4 ZIP64 archives, one per depth, 20 GeoTIFFs each (tiled, no overviews)activefile stem = layer nameruc-snapshot-2024-07-04WebDAV (Nextcloud), COGCOG, all 80 layers, snapshot 2024-07-04available80 files, all resolved
The download is four ZIP64 archives, one per depth, each with the 20 GeoTIFFs of that depth plus both reports and Danish and English READMEs. macOS’s Archive Utility and unzip report them as corrupt; they are not — extract with Python’s zipfile or 7-Zip, or read them in place with GDAL (/vsizip/…/depth_000_030_cm.zip/depth_000_030_cm/Clay_mean_000_030_cm.tif). The GeoTIFFs are tiled but have no overviews; the snapshot on the RUC data share (sgis-002180) has them as COGs, readable over the network.
A later, completed version exists. Gomes & Greve (2026) filled 42 166 ha of agricultural land that the 2024 mask left out (fields not cultivated in 2024), using a 101 × 101 focal mean of the surrounding cells — Tekstur2024_complete, delivered to SGAV in September 2026. Not on the hub as far as we know.

data/inner-workings/versions/vejstoej-st.title: Vejstøj, større byområder 2017
data/inner-workings/versions/vejstoej-st.content:
Version 2017 of Vejstøj, større byområder.
SGIS reference: sgis-000386
Abstract
Datasættet indeholder 8 featuretypes:
Veje i by, nat, 4 m
Veje i by, nat, 1,5 m
Veje i by, 4 m
Veje i by, 1,5 m
Større veje i by, nat, 4 m
Større veje i by, nat, 1,5 m
Større veje i by, 4 m
Større veje i by, 1,5 m

Kortlægning af veje i større, samlede byområder. I større, samlede byområder skal støjkortlægningen omfatte al vejstøj af betydning i kommunens område – også vejstøj, der hidrører fra statsveje i kommunen og eventuelt også bidrag fra stats- og kommuneveje beliggende i nabokommuner.
Kortlægning af statsveje. Vejdirektoratet gennemfører tilsvarende en kortlægning af alle større statsveje, der opfylder kriterierne >3 mio. køretøjer/år (> 8.000 ÅDT). Kortlægningen omfatter statsveje såvel indenfor som udenfor større, samlede byområder. Større statsveje i større, samlede byområder vil således blive kortlagt af både kommuner og af Vejdirektoratet.

data/inner-workings/versions/virksomheds.title: Virksomhedsstøj 2017
data/inner-workings/versions/virksomheds.content:
Version 2017 of Virksomhedsstøj.
SGIS reference: sgis-000666
Abstract
Datasættet indeholder 4 featuretypes:
Virksomheder i by, nat, 4 m
Virksomheder i by, nat, 1,5 m
Virksomheder i by, dag, 4 m
Virksomheder i by, nat, 1,5 m
Støjende virksomheder i byområder-. I henhold til forskrifterne i støjbekendtgørelsen skal der støjkortlægges for de (i)-mærkede virksomheder (IPPC-virksomheder), som giver anledning til støj i større, samlede byområder. Her ud over kan myndighederne vælge også at støjkortlægge andre, støjende virksomheder, som giver et væsentligt bidrag til støjbelastningen i byområderne. Det er dog alene relevant at kortlægge de virksomheder, der giver anledning til en støjbelastning, som er større end Lden = 55 dB eller Lnight = 50 dB i de pågældende byområder.
For Kommuner der er omfattet af direktiv 2002/49/EC

data/leaves/index.title: Leaves
data/leaves/index.content:
A leaf is a cognised existence — an abstract concept that exists independently of any particular dataset. Classically, GIS might call these “feature classes”, but that is too simplistic. A cognised existence names what something is (an address, a building, a service), then describes how it is realised by one or more datasets — including the spatial access paths (join chains) needed to reach geometry.
Leaves are the finest-grained navigable unit in the SPHERE protocol.
Why Leaves?
The same concept often spans multiple datasets. “Services” can be realised through CVR (filtering on branchekode), OpenStreetMap (amenity tags), or BBR (building use codes). A leaf isolates the concept and maps it to all its realisations with the specific entities, join chains, and coordinate representations each provides.
How to Read a Leaf
Each leaf tells you:

data/leaves/addresses.title: Addresses
data/leaves/addresses.content:
Cognised existence: An address is a structured spatial identifier that connects a human activity — dwelling, business, service — to a point in geographic space. It is a universal join key in many geospatial data ecosystems.

Question: Where is a property located by its official address?
What is an Address?
An address is not a coordinate. It is a layered set of identifiers (street name, house number, floor, door) that can collapse to one or more coordinate representations depending on purpose. In most data ecosystems, many registries reference addresses. Understanding the join chain from address entities to geometry is fundamental.
Realisations
Instead of hardcoding implementation schemas here, SPHERE separates semantic meaning from dataset implementation. The realisations are listed in priority order:


DAR Realisation (administrative_register)
OSM Realisation (volunteered)



Classical Theme References

data/leaves/administrative-units.title: Administrative Units
data/leaves/administrative-units.content:
Cognised existence: Administrative units are territorial divisions defined by governance acts. They exist because a political authority declared them. Their boundaries determine jurisdiction, statistical aggregation, electoral geography, and service responsibility.

Question: Which administrative area does a location belong to?
What is an Administrative Unit?
An administrative unit is an area with a name, a code, and a polygon boundary that groups other spatial objects (addresses, parcels, people, businesses) for governance purposes. Most countries have nested hierarchies (for example region → municipality → local district), often with parallel divisions for judicial, police, health, or electoral purposes.

Realisations
Instead of hardcoding implementation schemas here, SPHERE separates semantic meaning from dataset implementation. The realisations are listed in priority order:


DAGI (Danmarks Administrative Geografiske Inddeling) (administrative_register)
OpenStreetMap (volunteered)



Classical Theme References

data/leaves/bathing-water-quality.title: Bathing Water Quality
data/leaves/bathing-water-quality.content:

This leaf is intentionally multi-twig. It combines hydrological context, contamination indicators, exposure interpretation, and risk communication.
Core Question
Is bathing water suitable and safe for human recreational use at this location and time?
Why This Leaf Is Cross-Domain

Hydrosphere: the measured water body and station context
Hydrosphere Contaminants: pollutant and microbiological measurements in water
Anthroposphere Contaminants: human exposure interpretation

Hydrosphere -> Freshwater Surface Water
Hydrosphere -> Water Contaminants

Anthroposphere -> Services

data/leaves/buildings.content:

Question: What buildings exist at a location and what are their characteristics?
What is a Building?
A building combines two kinds of data: registry attributes (what it is, when it was built, how it’s used) and geometric footprint (its shape on the ground). These often come from different datasets. Understanding which to query depends on what you need.

data/leaves/business-financials.title: Economics and Employment
data/leaves/business-financials.content:
Cognised existence: Economics and employment describe the measurable scale of a firm’s activity — revenue, profit, assets, employment, and workforce intensity. The concept exists whether you read it from a company’s filed annual report or from an aggregated statistical table. The granularity and access differ dramatically between sources.

Question: What are the economic and employment characteristics of a firm or establishment?
What are Economics and Employment?
Economics and employment are not the firm itself (that’s Firms). They are the measurable scale and performance of the firm or establishment — how much money flows in, how many people work there, how large the asset base is, and how labor is distributed over time. Understanding which sources carry what level of detail, and what reporting obligations apply, is critical for avoiding false zeroes (missing ≠ zero).

data/leaves/business-locations.title: Business Locations
data/leaves/business-locations.content:
Cognised existence: A business location is the physical place where an enterprise conducts its activity — a shop, a factory floor, an office. It is not the business itself (that’s legal registration), not the building (that’s Buildings), and not the service provided (that’s Services). It is the operational presence of economic activity at a point in space.

Question: Where does a business physically operate?
What is a Business Location?
A business location answers “where is this enterprise, physically?” This is deceptively complex because a single company can have one registered office but dozens of production sites. Many national business registries separate these two concepts — and choosing the wrong one produces misleading maps.

Critical Distinction: Firm Address vs Production Unit

Always decide which address type matches your question before geocoding. For “where are the restaurants?”, you want production unit addresses. For “where is the company registered?”, you want firm addresses.

data/leaves/corporate-ownership.title: Ownership and Governance
data/leaves/corporate-ownership.content:
Cognised existence: Corporate ownership is the web of control relationships that connects natural persons and legal entities to the enterprises they own, govern, or benefit from. It is a directed graph — not a flat table — where chains of ownership can run through multiple intermediate companies before reaching a beneficial owner.

Question: Who owns, controls, or governs a firm?
What is Ownership and Governance?
Ownership and governance are not single attributes. They form a layered graph of legal ownership (who the registered owner is), beneficial ownership (who ultimately controls or benefits), capital relationships, and governance (who manages and makes decisions). Many regulatory frameworks distinguish these layers explicitly, and business registries often model them as separate entity types.

Realisations
Instead of hardcoding implementation schemas here, SPHERE separates semantic meaning from dataset implementation. The realisations are listed in priority order:


CVR (CentraleVirksomhedsregister) — Ownership Entities (administrative_register)



Why Only One Realisation?
Corporate ownership in Denmark is a legally defined relationship recorded exclusively in CVR by Erhvervsstyrelsen. Unlike addresses or buildings, there is no alternative data source that independently records who owns Danish companies. OSM does not capture ownership. DST publishes aggregated firm demographics but not ownership chains.
The EU Business Registers Interconnection System (BRIS) may eventually provide cross-border ownership data, but it is not yet integrated into the Danish data landscape.

data/leaves/economic-activities.title: Economic Activities
data/leaves/economic-activities.content:
Cognised existence: An economic activity is the classified function an enterprise performs — what it does in the economy. This concept exists independent of any particular register: a restaurant is a restaurant whether you read it from an industry code, an OSM amenity tag, or a statistical table.

Question: What economic activity does a business perform?
What is an Economic Activity?
An economic activity is not a business (that’s a legal entity). It is the type of work performed. A single enterprise may have multiple activities (primary + secondary). The classification enables sectoral analysis, economic diversity mapping, and filtering businesses by function.
For the legal business entity behind the activity, use Firms.
Different data sources encode this concept using incompatible taxonomies — business registries use industry code systems, OSM uses tag families, and statistics systems use aggregated sector classes. A leaf-level understanding lets an agent translate between them.

data/leaves/firms.title: Firms
data/leaves/firms.content:
Cognised existence: A firm is a legally recognized business entity that can own assets, incur obligations, report accounts, appoint management, and persist through time even as its activities, addresses, or establishments change.

Question: What firm is this, as a legal registered entity?
What is a Firm?
A firm is not an economic activity, not an establishment, and not a service. It is the legal business actor behind those other concepts. It has a stable identity, a legal form, a registration status, and a lifecycle. A single firm may operate many establishments, perform several activities, and hold ownership stakes in other firms.
This leaf is the right starting point when the user wants to identify a company, understand its legal structure, or anchor joins to other business-related concepts.

data/leaves/geotope.title: Geotope
data/leaves/geotope.content:
Cognised existence: a land unit that is internally homogeneous in its long-lasting (permanent) geoecological conditions — topography, topsoil and near-surface groundwater — and so offers one kind of potential for vegetation; separated from its neighbours by geotones, the zones where those conditions change. Defined by function (what it offers plants), not by genesis (how the landform was made) and not by current land use. (Christensen, Holmes & Nielsen 2026)

Question: Which parts of the landscape offer the same long-lasting conditions for plant life?
A geotope has a category (geotype; 16 in Region Zealand, from k-means) and attributes — the mean of each condition over its cells. So the leaf is a feature type whose features carry realisations of other leaves’ variables: SOC, clay, slope and groundwater depth per geotope.

Cognised existence: Orthoimagery is a geometrically corrected aerial or satellite photograph — the surface as seen from above, with positional accuracy. It is the most intuitive spatial data: it shows what the world looks like.

Not in a Sphere
Orthoimagery has no twig membership. An orthophoto is not about a theme: it is the product of a collection method, passive remote sensing, and it is the backdrop that other data is digitised from. Those digitised products, such as GeoDanmark buildings, are cartographic_compilation realisations with derived_from: [passive_rs]. Find imagery through Collection Methods or by search.
Thematic products interpreted from imagery, such as land cover classifications or NDVI, enter the network through their analytical focus. For example, land cover belongs to anthroposphere_perception_thematics and NDVI to biosphere_vegetation.

data/leaves/services.title: Services and Amenities
data/leaves/services.content:
Cognised existence: A service or amenity is a facility, institution, or establishment that provides a function to the public — healthcare, education, dining, retail, emergency response, recreation, or everyday convenience. The same concept is captured differently across datasets: as a business with an industry code, as a map point with an amenity tag, or as a building with a use code.

Question: What services or amenities are available at or near a location?
What is a Service or Amenity?
A service or amenity is not a building (that’s Buildings). It is not the legal business entity behind it (that’s Firms). It is the function provided at a place. A hospital provides healthcare. A school provides education. A restaurant provides dining. A playground provides recreation. The same physical building may house multiple services, and the same service type may appear across very different data sources.

Realisations
Instead of hardcoding implementation schemas here, SPHERE separates semantic meaning from dataset implementation. The realisations are listed in priority order:


CVR (CentraleVirksomhedsregister) — By Industry Code (administrative_register)
OpenStreetMap — By Amenity Tag (volunteered)
BBR (BygningerOgBoliger) — By Building Use Code (administrative_register)



Combining Realisations
The power of multi-source realisations: CVR gives you business attributes (opening year, employee count, revenue). OSM gives you direct coordinates and opening hours. BBR gives you physical building characteristics. An agent assembling a complete picture of “healthcare services in Copenhagen” can draw from all three.

data/leaves/statistical-units.title: Statistical Units
data/leaves/statistical-units.content:
Cognised existence: A statistical unit is a territory defined so that figures can be reported and compared: NUTS regions across Europe, municipalities as LAU, census tracts within a country. The unit’s ID is what statistical tables carry; the geometry is borrowed from a realisation of the unit at the scale the map needs.

Question: Which statistical unit does a location or a statistical figure belong to?

What is a Statistical Unit?
Statistics are published per unit ID, usually without geometry. A table of population per NUTS 3 region lists DK011, DK012 and so on; to map it, the IDs are joined to a geometry of the same NUTS version. The same unit exists at several scales, from detailed boundaries for local maps to strongly generalised ones for maps of Europe, and all of them share the ID.
Two things matter for a correct join:

The ID scheme: NUTS_ID, LAU_ID or a national code such as kommunekode.
The version: NUTS is revised every few years and IDs can change between versions; LAU changes yearly.

Data that refers to a statistical unit records both in its realisation as anchored_by.

data/reference_framework/administrative_.title: Administrative Units
data/reference_framework/administrative_.content:
Units of governance with a legal identity, such as regions, municipalities and parishes. Other data refers to them by their code: Danmarks Statistik tables per kommunekode, registers that record the municipality of a person or a company.
Sphere: Reference Framework
One identity, many geometries
The code is the reference; the boundary is one of several geometries for it. A Danish municipality has the full-resolution DAGI boundary for detailed mapping, and the same unit appears as a generalised boundary in Eurostat’s LAU at 1:1M. Each reference realisation lists its geometries per scale and version under reference_units, so a map can borrow the geometry that suits its scale.
Scope

Danish administrative units (DAGI): regions (regionskode), municipalities (kommunekode), parishes (sognekode), and police and judicial districts
Other countries’ administrative units, when the network grows beyond Denmark

Key Distinction: Administrative vs Statistical Units
A unit defined by law and governance belongs here. A unit defined for reporting statistics is a statistical unit. Some are both: in Denmark the Eurostat LAU units are the municipalities.

data/reference_framework/crs/index.title: Coordinate Reference Systems
data/reference_framework/crs/index.content:
Sphere: Reference Framework
Description
The Geospatial Reference Framework serves as the mathematical and legal substrate of the SPHERE Protocol. It provides the “Geometric DNA” for all entities by defining the specific Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS) and spatial protocols required for a Realization to be placed accurately in 3D/4D space.

Key Logic


Mathematical Substrate: This twig does not contain physical shapes (delineations); instead, it contains the mathematical rules that allow those shapes to exist and be interpreted by an AI.


CRS as Cognitive Entities: Each coordinate system (e.g., EPSG:25832) is treated as a Leaf, acting as a “Logical Interpreter” for datasets.


Authority Alignment: Every leaf in this twig is threaded to the Governance twig to ensure that the chosen “math” aligns with legal mandates (such as SDFI standards in Denmark or GISCO standards in the EU).



Representative Leaves (Mathematical Anchors)






























Leaf IDTitleIntent & Scopecrs_epsg_25832ETRS89 / UTM zone 32NThe official 2D horizontal grid for Danish administrative and high-precision cadastral data.crs_epsg_25832_dvr90ETRS89 + DVR90The 3D vertical realization using the Danish Vertical Reference 1990.crs_epsg_3035ETRS89-LAEA (Europe)The Lambert Azimuthal Equal Area projection used for continental-scale statistical comparisons and EU environmental reporting.crs_epsg_3857Web MercatorThe global standard for interactive web maps and visual navigation (Google Maps/OpenStreetMap perspective).

Standard Operational Attributes
To guide the AI in selecting the correct coordinate frame for a given task, each leaf contains the following:


Operational Scale: [Local, National, or Continental].


Spatial Coverage: The specific extent where the CRS is valid (e.g., “Denmark” or “Europe”).


Primary Intent: The target output type, such as Print, High-Precision Export, or Statistical Comparison.



Relational Threads


Mandated By: Threads to anthroposphere_governance to identify the Responsible Authority (e.g., SDFI, Eurostat, or EPSG) behind the coordinate definition.


Frames: Threads to Realizations to provide the necessary spatial reference for any incoming “Spade” (dataset).


Leaves

No leaves yet.

Height benchmarks: Levelling points realising the vertical datum (DVR90)
GNSS reference stations: Permanent stations and correction services
Tide gauges: As vertical reference for coastal and marine datums

data/reference_framework/grids_map_sheet.title: Grids and Map Sheets
data/reference_framework/grids_map_sheet.content:
Systematic partitions of space used to index and tile data, from the sheet divisions of historical map series to web tiling schemes.
Sphere: Reference Framework
Scope

National square grids used as an index: for example, the Danish Kvadratnet cell names (1 km, 10 km, 100 km)
Discrete global grid systems: H3, S2, DGGAL indices
Map sheet divisions: Current and historical sheet schemes (e.g., Historiske Kortbladsinddelinger), needed to locate scanned historical maps
Tiling schemes: Web map tile matrices used by tile services

Key Distinction: Indexing vs Reporting
A grid used to index or tile space belongs here. When the same grid is used as a statistical reporting unit (e.g., population per km² cell), it is a statistical unit. The predefined Danish and European statistical grids, and how to align an ad hoc grid with them, are described under Statistical grids.

data/reference_framework/index.title: Reference Framework
data/reference_framework/index.content:
Description: The Reference Framework is not a thematic sphere. It holds what other data is located by. There are two kinds of reference:

Coordinate frames: coordinate reference systems and the geodetic points that realise them. Data with its own coordinates is positioned through these.
Reference units: stable identities that other data refers to by ID, such as municipalities, NUTS regions, statistical units and addresses. Non-spatial data, for example a table of population per municipality, carries only the ID and borrows the geometry from here.


One identity, many geometries. A reference unit keeps its ID while its geometry exists in several versions for different scales. The Danish municipality 0101 has a full-resolution DAGI boundary and a generalised Eurostat LAU boundary at 1:1M. The NUTS region DK01 exists at 1:1M, 1:3M, 1:10M, 1:20M and 1:60M. Reference realisations record their ID scheme and their geometries per scale and version (reference_units). Data that refers to them records which unit and ID scheme it uses (anchored_by).
Subclasses (Complexes):

reference_crs: Coordinate reference systems and vertical datums (e.g., EPSG:25832, DVR90, ETRS89-LAEA).
reference_geodetic_control: Physical points that realise the reference systems (e.g., geodetic control points, benchmarks, GNSS reference stations).
reference_administrative_units: Units of governance with a legal ID (e.g., Danish regions, municipalities and parishes from DAGI).
reference_statistical_units: Units defined for reporting statistics (e.g., NUTS, LAU, census tracts, statistical grids).
reference_addresses: Official addresses and access points, the finest unit most registers refer to.
reference_grids_map_sheets: Systematic partitions used to index and tile space (e.g., map sheet divisions, tiling schemes, DGGS indices).


Common Overlaps & Distinctions:

Frame vs Theme: A leaf belongs here when its purpose is to locate or frame other data, not to describe a phenomenon. A DTM describes the land surface, so it belongs to geosphere_landform_topography.
Not imagery: Orthophotos and satellite imagery are a collection method (passive remote sensing), not a reference. See Passive Remote Sensing and the Orthoimagery leaf.
Authority: Reference units are mandated by authorities (SDFI, Danmarks Statistik, Eurostat). Leaves here often also belong to anthroposphere_governance.
Statistical vs indexing grids: A grid used to report statistics (e.g., population per km² cell) is a statistical unit. A grid used to index or tile space belongs to Grids and Map Sheets.



Leaves

data/reference_framework/statistical_uni.title: Statistical Units
data/reference_framework/statistical_uni.content:
Units defined for reporting statistics. Statistical tables are usually published per unit ID without geometry: a population figure for NUTS region DK01, an indicator per LAU. The geometry is borrowed from a reference realisation of the unit, at whatever scale suits the map.
Sphere: Reference Framework
One identity, many geometries
Eurostat publishes NUTS for each version (2016, 2021, 2024) at five scales, 1:1M, 1:3M, 1:10M, 1:20M and 1:60M, all sharing the same NUTS_ID. LAU is published yearly at 1:1M. IDs can change between versions, so a statistical table must state which version its IDs refer to.
Scope

NUTS (Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics): levels 0–3 for the EU and EFTA
LAU (Local Administrative Units): the municipal level below NUTS 3; in Denmark the municipalities
Census tracts and enumeration areas: national units such as the UK’s census output areas
Statistical grids: square cells used for reporting, such as Danmarks Statistik’s km² grid and the INSPIRE/Eurostat 1 km grid

Statistical grids: predefined and ad hoc
A grid of equal cells makes zones that do not change when administrative borders do, and that can be compared between places and years. Two grids are predefined for Denmark:

Det Danske Kvadratnet (the Danish square grid), defined in 2001 by Kort- og Matrikelstyrelsen (now Klimadatastyrelsen) and Danmarks Statistik. Square cells from 100 m to 100 km in EUREF89 UTM zone 32 (EPSG:25832). A cell is named by its size and its lower-left corner, truncated to the cell size: the 1 km cell containing N 6188431, E 709802 is 1km_6188_709. A coordinate therefore gives its cell without an overlay, and the cells nest: one 10 km cell holds a hundred 1 km cells. Danmarks Statistik publishes grid statistics on it. Source: Dataforsyningen.
The European statistical grid (GISCO/INSPIRE), from Eurostat: square cells of 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100 km in ETRS89-LAEA (EPSG:3035), covering Europe, with census population for 2006, 2011, 2018 and 2021. Source: Eurostat GISCO grids.

The two grids do not line up: they are square in different projections, so a Danish cell and a European cell of the same size cut across each other. Choose the one whose statistics you compare with.
An ad hoc grid is generated for the study (generate grid): a cell size or shape no predefined grid offers, such as 250 m squares or hexagons. Recommendations:

If a predefined grid fits the question, use it, or generate a grid that is aligned with it exactly: the same CRS, an origin on its corner values, and a cell size that divides into its cells. Results can then be compared with official statistics and other studies, and summed to the predefined cells.
If the cells must be hexagons — for neighbourhood, movement or connectivity — accept that they cannot be compared cell by cell with official statistics; see Square and hexagonal grids.
Record the cell size, shape, origin and CRS: they are choices that shape the result (the scale and zoning effects of the Modifiable areal unit problem).

Leaves

data/sphere.title: SPHERE: Semantic Protocol for Human and Earth Relational Environments
data/sphere.content:
Semantic Protocol for Human and Earth Relational Environments
SPHERE is the organising protocol behind this site. It structures how heterogeneous datasets—registries that serve many domains at once—are decomposed into discoverable, purpose-specific units that both humans and AI agents can navigate.
The Problem
A registry like CVR contains 27 object classes and 361 attributes. It serves questions about industry classification, spatial footprint, ownership structure, financial health, and more. No single description captures all of these purposes. An agent asking “where are Copenhagen’s restaurants?” needs different metadata than one asking “who owns this company?”—yet both draw from the same registry.
Flat dataset catalogs force a choice: either one monolithic description per registry (too broad) or one page per entity (too low-level). Neither matches how questions are actually asked.
A Network, Not a Tree
SPHERE was first drawn as a tree crown: spheres as branches, twigs within them, and leaves hanging from one twig each. In practice the data is a network. A Natura 2000 designation is as much a planning instrument as an ecosystem; a drinking water protection zone is planning, groundwater, and resource use at once. Forcing each leaf onto a single branch hid exactly the connections that matter. The names of the elements are kept, but their relations are those of a network:



































ElementRole in the networkExampleSphereA thematic hub—a cluster of related phenomenaAnthroposphere, Hydrosphere, BiosphereTwigA narrower hub within a spherePlanning, Groundwater, EcosystemsLeafA node: a semantic aspect of a dataset that answers one kind of question”Drinking Water Protection”MembershipAn edge from a leaf to every twig it is relevant toDrinking Water Protection → Planning, Groundwater, Resource UtilisationThreadA membership that carries an explicit rationaleIndustry codes → Biosphere Ecosystems, because they signal environmental pressure
A leaf may name one membership as its primary lens, the preferred entry point for navigation. Leaves that are cross-domain by nature have no primary lens, and no membership is second-class: a twig page lists every leaf that is a member.
The protocol has 5 thematic spheres—Atmosphere, Biosphere, Hydrosphere (including the cryosphere), Geosphere (rock and soil, formerly Lithosphere and Pedosphere), and Anthroposphere (formerly Socio-Technical)—plus the non-thematic Reference Framework (coordinate frames, and the reference units such as municipalities, NUTS regions and addresses that other data refers to by ID). The spheres originate in the geoilum analysis project, where they balanced variables so no domain was over-represented; they were reorganised in 2026 for data organisation.
Two axes run across the spheres:

What a leaf is about: its twig memberships.
How the data was produced: the collection_method of each realisation (register, in-situ, passive or active remote sensing, derived/modelled, volunteered, cartographic). Remote-sensed data therefore enters the network through its analytical focus, not through a “remote sensing” sphere.

How it works

Spheres and twigs are the hubs (→ SPHERE)
Leaves decompose registries into purpose-specific semantic aspects and link to every relevant twig (→ Leaves)
Each leaf points down to Realisations, which map it onto Dataset documentation (→ Data/Inner workings/Schemas/Schemas) and Services (GraphQL, WFS, file download)
Threads explain the memberships that are not self-evident, enabling lateral discovery

The Architecture Chain
Leaf (semantic aspect, answers a question type)
  → Realisation (implementation mapping, join logic, dataset choice)
    → Dataset (registry info, license, temporal model)
      → Service (GraphQL endpoint, WFS, file download, API key)

An agent navigating SPHERE:

Identifies the sphere or twig matching its question domain
Browses the leaves connected to that twig—including those whose primary lens is elsewhere
Identifies the realisation that best fits its technical or authoritative requirements
Follows the realisation’s mapping and join logic to the dataset documentation
Uses service references to access the actual data

Leaf Schema
Every leaf page uses this frontmatter structure:
---
title: <human-readable leaf name>
type: leaf
draft: false
twig_membership:
  - <every twig this leaf is relevant to>
primary_lens: <optional; one of twig_membership>
concept: <semantic concept from the collection's semantic organisation>
question: <what kind of question does this leaf help answer?>
threads:
  - <thread ids: memberships that carry an explicit rationale>
tags:
  - collection/<collection-slug>
---
Memberships and Threads: Cross-Domain Connections
Many phenomena sit at the boundary between spheres. Industry codes in CVR classify economic activity (Anthroposphere) but also signal environmental impact (Biosphere) and thematic human partitioning of space (Anthroposphere Perception & Thematics). Rather than duplicating leaves, a leaf simply has a membership in every twig it is relevant to. Where the reason for a membership is not obvious, a thread records it.
An agent exploring the Biosphere finds CVR industry classification listed on the Ecosystems twig, as a member like any other.
For the conventions on memberships, primary lenses, and threads, see SPHERE Thread Conventions.
Backward Compatibility
The existing 338+ pages in Data/Inner workings/Schemas/Schemas and SPHERE remain unchanged. They form the Dataset tier of the architecture chain. Leaves add a new semantic layer on top, linking down to those pages. Nothing is removed or reorganised.
Classical Metadata Standards
Three widely-used geospatial classification systems — ISO 19115, INSPIRE, and UN-GGIM — define flat lists of topic categories. SPHERE maps all 67 classical themes into the network, providing a Rosetta Stone between legacy catalog keywords and the sphere/twig/thread structure. This enables systematic harvesting from existing metadata servers.
See Classical Classifications → SPHERE Mapping for the full concordance.
Navigation





























Starting pointPathI have a question about a domainSPHERE → find sphere → twig → browse member leavesI know the registryData/Inner workings/Schemas/Schemas → registry page → follow leaf backlinksI want to browse all semantic aspectsAll LeavesI have a classical metadata keyword (ISO/INSPIRE/UN-GGIM)Classical Classifications → find theme → follow to sphereI want the protocol definitionYou are here
Status
SPHERE is in pilot phase. The first leaves cover CVR as a proof of concept, decomposing it into four semantic aspects: industry classification, spatial footprint, ownership structure, and financial profile.
Machine-Readable Discovery
For programmatic agent access, the full sphere/twig/leaf/thread network is available as a JSON index:

Sphere index: sphere-index.v1.json

This file contains all spheres, leaves with their entities and key attributes, service pointers, and thread cross-references. Agents can fetch this single file to discover everything available.

data/sphere/anthroposphere/index.title: Anthroposphere
data/sphere/anthroposphere/index.content:
Description: This sphere encompasses the human-created systems and organisational structures that shape environments and human activities. It includes infrastructure, services, socioeconomic patterns, governance, planning, digital and movement flows, thematic human perception, informal systems, the quantification of human resource utilisation, and human-centric risk. It was previously called Socio-Technical.
Subclasses (Complexes):

anthroposphere_infrastructure: Physical and organisational networks enabling urban and rural functions (e.g., transportation networks, utility grids, built environment as infrastructure, water/wastewater/stormwater infrastructure, waste management facilities).
anthroposphere_services: Organised activities and institutions providing essential functions (e.g., healthcare, education, public safety, commercial services, water supply/wastewater treatment services, energy generation/distribution).
anthroposphere_socioeconomic: Data on human populations, their activities, and organization (e.g., demographics, economy, land ownership, consumption patterns, general human population distribution, workforce data, GDP, income levels).
anthroposphere_governance: The administrative and legal framework: authorities, cadastral parcels, political divisions, environmental regulations, resource permits, fishing quotas, and the governance side of administrative units and addresses (as reference units these belong to the Reference Framework).
anthroposphere_planning: Human intent applied to space (e.g., spatial plans and zoning, planning decisions, nature and water protection designations, fisheries and forest management plans, marine spatial plans).
anthroposphere_ict_flows: Information and communication technologies and flow traces (e.g., sensor streams, digital platforms, communication infrastructure, movement telemetry).
anthroposphere_perception_thematics: Human thematic partitioning and cognitive map products (e.g., topographic/thematic maps, zoning interpretation layers, subjective classification views).
anthroposphere_informal_ephemeral: Informal, tactical, and short-lived human systems not consistently registered in formal cadastres or registries.
anthroposphere_contaminants: Data related to human-generated sources or pathways of contamination, or human exposure to contaminants and human health impacts (e.g., industrial emission points, hazardous waste sites, pollution regulations, spatial distribution of human disease cases/outbreaks, human exposure assessment data).
anthroposphere_hazard_vulnerability_risk: Data combining natural or anthropocentric hazards with human vulnerability and exposure, leading to comprehensive risk assessments and management strategies. This includes spatial data on population vulnerability, critical infrastructure exposure, and multi-hazard risk mapping. Note: This is the risk to humans, not the natural hazard itself.
anthroposphere_resource_utilisation: Data on the direct physical quantification of human resource extraction, harvesting, consumption, and production from natural systems. This includes measured volumes of abstracted water, harvested biomass (e.g., fish catches, timber yields), mineral extraction quantities, and energy production from natural sources.

data/sphere/anthroposphere/contaminants/.title: Contaminants (Human Exposure)
data/sphere/anthroposphere/contaminants/.content:
Data on human-generated contamination sources, pathways of human exposure, and health impacts. Every sphere has its own contaminants subclass for pollutants within that medium — this twig specifically addresses the human side: where contamination originates from human activity and how it affects human populations.
Scope

Industrial emission points: Factory stacks, discharge pipes, point-source pollution locations
Hazardous waste sites: Contaminated land registries, brownfield databases
Pollution regulations: Emission permits, discharge limits, compliance monitoring
Human disease distribution: Spatial epidemiology, disease clusters, health exposure mapping
Human exposure assessment: Dose-response models, proximity analysis to contamination sources

Distinction from Other Contaminant Subclasses
Each sphere has a _contaminants subclass — but they describe different things:

Atmosphere contaminants: Pollutants in the air (NO₂, PM2.5)
Hydrosphere contaminants: Pollutants in water (heavy metals, microplastics)
Anthroposphere contaminants: The human source and human impact — where pollution comes from, and what it does to people
