Audit (Task Schema step 2)
Processing Toolbox › Vector analysis › Basic statistics for fields on the criterion: count, number of empty values, minimum, maximum, mean, median, quartiles. Sort the attribute table by the field, both ways, and look at the units at each end.
Hold out (step 3)
Field calculator (Tool - QGIS), a decimal field, e.g. x_clean:
if(<condition for not applicable>, NULL, "x")

e.g. if("regareal" = "vejareal" OR "adresser" IS NULL, NULL, "kvm_pr:adresse"). Score from x_clean from then on.
Score (step 4)
Field calculator (Tool - QGIS), a decimal field per score. The aggregate functions (maximum, minimum, mean, stdev, count) skip NULLs; stdev is the sample standard deviation.





































FunctionExpressiondivide by the maximum100 * "x" / maximum("x")min–max100 * ("x" - minimum("x")) / (maximum("x") - minimum("x"))z-score("x" - mean("x")) / stdev("x")log, then min–max100 * (ln("x" + 1) - minimum(ln("x" + 1))) / (maximum(ln("x" + 1)) - minimum(ln("x" + 1)))thresholds, linear betweenscale_linear("x", <a>, <b>, 100, 0): 100 up to a, 0 beyond b (for a distance to something good); scale_linear("x", <a>, <b>, 0, 100) where high values are gooddistance decayif("x" IS NULL, NULL, 100 * exp(-"x" / <d>))lookup tableCASE WHEN "class" IN ('1','2','3') THEN 0 WHEN "class" IN ('4','5','6') THEN 50 WHEN "class" IN ('7','8','9') THEN 100 ELSE NULL END
scale_linear clamps: values below a get the score at a, values beyond b the score at b. The if(… IS NULL, NULL, …) around the distance decay is needed because exp(NULL) returns 1, which would give a missing distance the score 100.
Percentile rank takes two steps:

Add autoincremental field (Tool - QGIS): Field name r_x, Start values at 1, Sort expression "x", Sort ascending on, Sort nulls first off.
Field calculator (Tool - QGIS): if("x" IS NULL, NULL, 100 * mean("r_x", group_by:="x") / count("x")). Equal values get their mean rank; count("x") counts only values that are not NULL. On 34,000 parcels this step takes a few minutes per criterion.

Direction (step 5)
Reverse a score where high raw values are bad: 100 - "score_x", or give it a negative weight in the weighted sum. Not both.
Check (step 6)
Basic statistics for fields on the score: the median and standard deviation, and the number of NULLs, which should equal the number of held-out units. Statistics by categories on the score shows how many units share one value.
Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Recipes/Site plan and concept diagrams (Recipe - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Site plan and concept diagrams (Recipe — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
Used in Urban Design Visualisation (Example) (step 3). Applies Visual hierarchy and figure-ground: white buildings, soft shadows, faint contours, and colour only in the design.
Turn the orthophoto off before you export anything.
1. Style the context layers





























LayerStyleBuildingsFill white, outline black 0.25–0.35 mm. Layer Styling → Draw effects → Drop shadow: grey, offset 2–4 mm, blur 3–5Ground surfacesThe polygons from Surface partitioning (Recipe - QGIS), one pale fill per classContoursFrom the DTM: Raster → Extraction → Contour, interval 0.25–0.5 m. Thin light grey lines (0.1 mm, 40% opacity)Hillshade (optional)Raster → Analysis → Hillshade, at 10–20% opacity under everythingExisting treesPoints with a simple circle or SVG tree symbol, grey-green, with drop shadow
The drop shadow here is a graphic convention, not a claim about the sun. For sun-correct shadows, see Line drawings and shadow plans (Recipe - Blender).
2. Draw the proposal
Create a GeoPackage 02_qgis/design.gpkg with separate layers for planting, water, paving zones, furniture and new trees. These layers carry the colour, texture and detail: planting in soft greens, water in dark blue, paving as fine patterns.
3. Print layout

Project → New Print Layout. Page A3 landscape, map at 1:500 (or 1:400 for a close-up).
Add a north arrow, a scale bar and a few labels in a serif or plain sans font. Leave white space.
Export as SVG or PDF (Layout → Export as SVG/PDF) and finish in Affinity — textures, people from above, text. See A0 poster layout (Recipe - Affinity).

4. Concept diagrams
Make a copy of the layout. Show the square as one flat light-grey surface with a thick black outline and hide almost everything else. On top, add:

Zones as transparent colour polygons (30–50% opacity, one colour each)
Flows and connections as lines with an arrow symbol layer (Symbol layer type → Arrow)
Three or four diagrams side by side, each making one point

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Recipes/Site screening by criteria (Recipe - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Site screening by criteria (Recipe — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
Tool-bound implementation of the Site screening by criteria (Task) Task Schema in QGIS 4.2. Worked example: Sites for new housing near stations in Copenhagen (Example).
Data you need









































RoleFormLevel of measurementNotesCandidate unitspolygonsattributes used in conditions: anye.g. parcels with area and number of addressesLayers to be nearpoints, lines or polygonstype field: nominale.g. stationsLayers that excludepoints or polygonsprotection status: nominal; protection class: ordinale.g. protected buildingsLayers to cut awaypolygons—e.g. parksSites (output)polygonsthe units that pass every criterion
All layers in the same projected CRS, so that distances and areas are in metres.
Conditions on the units’ own attributes (Task Schema steps 2–3)
Extract by expression (Tool - QGIS) on the candidate units, one condition per run so that you can count after each, e.g.
"<type field>" = '<value>'
"<area per address field>" >= <threshold> OR "<address count field>" IS NULL

A field name with an unusual character, such as kvm_pr:adresse, works in double quotes. Check the field type in the layer’s properties: a class stored as text is compared as text, "<class field>" IN ('1','2','3').
Near another layer (step 3)

If only some features count, extract them first with Extract by expression (Tool - QGIS), e.g. "<type field>" IN ('<type 1>','<type 2>').
Buffer (Tool - QGIS): Distance the threshold in metres, Dissolve result on.
Processing Toolbox › Vector selection › Extract by location: Extract features from the units, Where the features intersect, By comparing to features from the buffer.

Away from another layer (step 3)

Extract the features that exclude, e.g. "<status field>" = '<protected>' OR "<class field>" IN ('1','2','3').
Extract by location: Where the features are disjoint, By comparing to features from the excluding layer.

Cutting parts away (step 3)
Difference (Tool - QGIS): Input layer the units, Overlay layer the layer to cut away. Each unit keeps its attributes but loses the part inside the overlay. Units entirely inside disappear.
Size criteria last (step 5)
Extract by expression (Tool - QGIS): area(@geometry) >= <minimum m²>. area(@geometry) measures in the layer’s CRS; $area measures on the ellipsoid set in the project and gives slightly different values.
Check (steps 4 and 6)
Note the feature count after every step (Show feature count in the Layers panel), in a table with the criterion and its threshold. Then sort the result by area and look at the largest sites over an orthophoto or a basemap.
Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Recipes/Slope and flow direction from DHM (Recipe - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Slope and Flow Direction from DHM (Recipe — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
Tool-bound implementation of the Slope and flow direction (Task) Task Schema.

Editorial note: the processing steps below were run end to end in QGIS 4.2.2 (headless, 8 October 2026) on a 2 × 2 km window around Himmelbjerget, using the DHM WCS from Datafordeleren. The menu paths are written from QGIS conventions; check the wording against your own QGIS version.

Load the terrain model (Task Schema step 1)
With the SemanticGIS plugin: Elevation › Datafordeleren: Danmarks Højdemodel (DHM) › DHM WCS › dhm_terraen (double-click). It needs your own Datafordeleren API key in the plugin settings. dhm_terraen is the terrain model (DTM); dhm_overflade is the surface model (DSM) and is not the right input here.
Without the plugin: Layer → Data Source Manager → WCS, a new connection with the URL wcs.datafordeler.dk/DHMNedboer/dhm_wcs/1.0.0/WCS key>, then the coverage dhm_terraen.
The layer shows heights in metres. Check with the Identify tool: Himmelbjerget’s summit reads about 146.7 m.
Save a local copy (Task Schema step 2)
Zoom to the study area plus a margin. Right-click the WCS layer → Export → Save As…:

Format: GeoTIFF
CRS: EPSG:25832 — the coverage’s own system; do not reproject a height model before analysis
Extent: Map Canvas Extent, or type the coordinates
Resolution: horizontal and vertical 1.6 (m) for landscape scale, or 0.4 for the full detail (16 times as many cells)

The test window (542000–544000 E, 6217000–6219000 N) at 1.6 m gave 1,250 × 1,250 cells, heights 20.8 m (Julsø) to 158.1 m, in about 4 seconds.
Fill sinks and get flow directions (Task Schema steps 3 and 5)
Processing Toolbox → Fill sinks (Wang & Liu) (native:fillsinkswangliu; native in QGIS 4, formerly a SAGA tool):

Input layer: the local GeoTIFF
Minimum slope (degrees): 0.01
Outputs: the filled DEM, flow directions and watershed basins

The flow-direction raster codes the direction to the steepest downhill neighbour, clockwise from north:



























Code01234567DirectionNNEESESSWWNW
(Verified on the test window: the code matched the steepest-descent neighbour in 98% of cells; the rest are flats and ties.) Style it with Paletted/Unique values and eight colours.
Compute slope (Task Schema step 4)
Processing Toolbox → Raster terrain analysis → Slope (native:slope): input the filled DEM (or the local DTM if you are not doing flow analysis), Z factor 1. The output is in degrees. The test window ranged from 0 to 52.7°, with a mean of 9.4° (the steep slopes are the valley sides around Julsø).
Optional: flow accumulation (Task Schema step 6)
GRASS r.watershed (grass:r.watershed) on the filled DEM gives flow accumulation and stream segments; tick Single Flow Direction (D8) to match the flow directions above. It needs a QGIS installation with GRASS, which not every QGIS 4 package includes; the test installation did not have it.
ArcGIS
(To fill in: the equivalent in ArcGIS Pro — Fill, Flow Direction and Slope in the Spatial Analyst toolbox; same Task Schema. Note that ArcGIS codes D8 directions as powers of two, 1 = E … 128 = NE, not 0–7.)

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Recipes/Surface partitioning (Recipe - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Surface partitioning (Recipe — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
Tool-bound implementation of the Surface partitioning (Task) Schema, for GeoDanmark data. Uses the Surface partition tools of the SemanticGIS plugin; the data comes from step 2 of Building heights from DHM (Recipe - QGIS). Used in Urban Design Visualisation (Example) (step 2).
GeoDanmark has road edges (Vejkant) and centre lines (Vejmidte), but no area polygons for roads, pavements, cycle paths or plazas. They are built in three steps.
A — Collect the edges
Keep Road centre lines (Vejmidte) switched off (centre lines must not become boundaries) and keep the kerbs (Vejkant), the buildings and any other edge layers visible. Run SemanticGIS › Vector geometry › Surface partition 1: build lines with your study area and snap tolerance 0.3 m. Save both outputs in 02_qgis/context.gpkg:

Partition lines — all edges as one line layer, split where they cross. The field src_layer shows where each line came from.
Gaps (loose line ends) — points at loose line ends: the gaps that stop areas from closing.

B — Clean up by hand
Turn on snapping (Project → Snapping Options, vertex and segment, 1 m). Edit the partition lines:

Close each gap at a loose end with a short line.
Delete overshoots that stick out past a crossing.
Draw the boundaries the data lacks, e.g. the edge between a plaza and the pavement, or the kerb of a planting bed.

C — Make polygons
Run SemanticGIS › Vector geometry › Surface partition 2: polygons from lines:

Input: the edited partition lines
Buildings: the clipped building layer (polygons inside buildings become building)
Centre lines: Vejmidte, and its road-type field as a hint
Output: 02_qgis/context.gpkg, layer surfaces

If an area is missing, there is still a gap: check the Remaining gaps output, fix the lines, and run step C again.
D — Classify
Open the attribute table, use the hint column as a guide, and set surface from the drop-down (road, cycle path, footpath / pavement, plaza, parking, green, water, building, other). Unclassified polygons are outlined in red. Precision matters only in and around the square; the rest of the study area can be rough.
To save the drop-down and colours with the layer: Layer Properties → Style → Save as Default (stored in the GeoPackage).
Troubleshooting




















ProblemCauseFixAn area is missing after Surface partition 2A gap in the partition linesLook at the Remaining gaps points, close the gap with snapping on, run Surface partition 2 againRoad cut into many small piecesVejmidte was visible in Surface partition 1Hide centre lines and run Surface partition 1 again, or delete the centre lines from the partition layer

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Recipes/Vegetation index from Sentinel-2 (Recipe - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Vegetation index from Sentinel-2 (Recipe — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
Tool-bound implementation of the Vegetation index from satellite imagery (Task) Task Schema with the Copernicus Browser and QGIS 4.2. Worked example: Vegetation greenness at Ledreborg (Example).
Data you need









































RoleFormLevel of measurementNotesStudy areapolygon—as WKT or GeoJSON in EPSG:4326 for the Browser, or drawn thereRed and near infraredraster, one band eachratioSentinel-2 L2A B04 and B08, 10 m, surface reflectanceScene classification (optional)rasternominalSentinel-2 L2A SCL: 4 vegetation, 5 not vegetated, 6 water; 3 cloud shadow, 8–10 cloud and cirrus. Not a raw band in the Copernicus Browser; from the original L2A productBlue and green (optional)raster, one band eachratioB02, B03, for true-colour and colour-infrared imagesNDVI (output)raster, 32-bit floatratio (−1 to 1)

The Copernicus Browser’s download set up for NDVI: Analytical, TIFF (16-bit), custom resolution 10 m, UTM 32N, raw bands B04 and B08.
Find and download the image (Task Schema steps 1–3)

Make the study area into WKT in WGS 84: Processing Toolbox › SemanticGIS › Vector geometry › Area of interest as WKT (WGS 84), shape Bounding box, a buffer of e.g. 200 m. The WKT is copied to the clipboard. Without the SemanticGIS plugin: right-click the layer › Export › Save Features As…, format GeoJSON, CRS EPSG:4326.
In the Copernicus Browser, log in, and add the area with the area-of-interest tool (polygon icon, top right): paste the WKT or upload the GeoJSON, or draw a rectangle.
Search (Tool - Copernicus Browser): SEARCH tab, Sentinel-2 › MSI › L2A, a time range in the season the question needs, Search.
Go through the results with Visualize. Choose a date with no cloud over the study area itself, whatever the cloud cover figure says.
Download image (Tool - Copernicus Browser), tab Analytical (Show more for all options): image format TIFF (16-bit) or TIFF (32-bit float), image resolution CUSTOM with 10 m/px in X and Y, coordinate system UTM 32N (EPSG:32632), under Raw tick B04 and B08 (and B02, B03 for the colour images). Download and unzip into the project folder.

Look at the values and the image (steps 4–5)

Add the GeoTIFFs to QGIS. Check with Identify Features on a field or wood: in 32-bit float B04 is about 0.02–0.05 and B08 about 0.3–0.5 (in 16-bit about 200–500 and 3000–5000). From the Browser there is no offset to remove.
True colour: Build virtual raster (Tool - QGIS) with B04, B03, B02 in that order, Place each input file into a separate band ticked; Symbology › Multiband color, Red = Band 1, Green = Band 2, Blue = Band 3. Colour infrared: the same with B08, B04, B03. Look for cloud, haze and shadow.

Calculate and mask NDVI (steps 6–7)


Raster calculator (Tool - QGIS) (Raster › Raster Calculator…), with the band names as they appear in your Layers panel:
("B08@1" - "B04@1") / ("B08@1" + "B04@1")

With a scene classification (SCL) from the original L2A product, clouds and shadows can be masked:
( ("B08@1" - "B04@1") / ("B08@1" + "B04@1") ) / ( "SCL@1" = 4 OR "SCL@1" = 5 OR "SCL@1" = 6 )

The part after the middle / is the mask: it is 1 for vegetation, bare surface and water and 0 for everything else, and dividing by 0 gives NoData. From the Copernicus Browser there is no SCL band, so choose a date without cloud over the study area (step 4).


Symbology › Singleband pseudocolor, min −0.2, max 1, colour ramp RdYlGn; or Discrete with classes at 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8.


Check (step 8)

Layer Properties › Information or Raster layer statistics (Raster analysis): minimum and maximum between −1 and 1. NDVI above 1 means an offset has been subtracted that was not there, or not subtracted where it was (an original .SAFE product: subtract 1000 from each band first).
Identify a few known surfaces: a lake below 0 (if open water fills a whole pixel), a road or roof near 0–0.3, forest and crops in June 0.8–0.9.

Summarise (step 9)

Per zone: Zonal statistics (Tool - QGIS); per land-use class: Raster layer zonal statistics, as in Aggregating a continuous raster to zones (Recipe - QGIS).

Check numbers
With the Ledreborg example (14 June 2025): mean NDVI 0.81, median 0.87, 74 % of the cells above 0.8; the mask removes 696 cells (0.2 %).
QGIS steps checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Copernicus Browser steps written from the Browser’s documentation; labels can change.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/SemanticGIS plugin.md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: SemanticGIS plugin for QGIS
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
The SemanticGIS plugin brings the data network of this site into QGIS. You browse it the same way as on the website, and a double-click on a service adds it as a layer.
What it does

Browse the data network. The panel has the same seven entrances as Data on this site: SPHERE, Classical Classifications (INSPIRE, ISO 19115, UN-GGIM), Collection Methods, Datasets by Collection, Datasets by Owner, the Reference Framework and Basemaps. Leaves and datasets can be searched.
Add layers. WFS, WMS, WMTS, WCS and XYZ services are added with one double-click. When several providers serve the same dataset, the preferred and verified service is marked ★.
Keep the provenance. Every layer is grouped under its leaf and tagged with the leaf, dataset and service it came from, so a saved project still knows where its data came from.
Credit the data. Every layer carries its attribution line, and Copy attributions for the map gives the lines for a print layout.
Join a table to reference units. A statistics table with unit IDs or names, such as municipality codes or NUTS codes, gets the geometry of the matching units.
Processing tools. The plugin adds tools to the Processing Toolbox under SemanticGIS, among them Tabulate area and Zonal statistics by class, which use the legend labels of a categorical raster in their output. For urban design, Urban context for a study area fetches GeoDanmark and building heights from Danmarks Højdemodel for a study area in one step; Building heights, Clip project layers to one GeoPackage and Surface partition do the single steps (see Building heights from DHM (Recipe - QGIS)).
Show web page. Every item in the panel opens its page on this site.

Installing
The plugin is not in the official QGIS plugin repository yet. It is installed from its own channel:

In QGIS, open Plugins › Manage and Install Plugins › Settings, click Add…, give the channel a name (for example SemanticGIS) and paste this address:
raw.githubusercontent.com/Esbern/semanticGIS-qgis/plugin-repository/stable.xml
Find SemanticGIS under All and click Install Plugin. New versions then appear under Upgradeable.
Open the panel from Web › SemanticGIS.

See Managing QGIS plugins for the Plugin Manager in general. The source code and a full description are on GitHub.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Add autoincremental field (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Add autoincremental field (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector table › Add autoincremental field (native:addautoincrementalfield).
Realises:

Rank, through Sort expression
the first half of a percentile rank

Settings that matter

Field name and Start values at: 1 gives ranks from 1.
Sort expression: the field to rank by, e.g. "suitability". Without it, the numbers follow the order of the features in the layer and mean nothing.
Sort ascending: off for a rank where the highest value gets 1; on for a percentile rank, where the lowest value gets 1.
Group values by: numbers each group from the start value, e.g. a rank within each district.

Watch out

Equal values get consecutive numbers in an arbitrary order. For a percentile rank, give ties their mean rank afterwards with the Field calculator (Tool - QGIS): 100 * mean("r", group_by:="x") / count("r").
The numbers are fixed when the tool runs. Change a weight and the rank must be computed again.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Buffer (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Buffer (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector geometry › Buffer (native:buffer); menu: Vector › Geoprocessing Tools › Buffer.
Realises:

Dilation — with a positive Distance
Erosion — with a negative Distance
Dissolve — with Dissolve result ticked
Explode — with Keep disjoint results separate ticked as well (QGIS 4.2; not in older releases)

Settings that matter

Distance is in the layer’s units: metres in EPSG:25832, but degrees if the layer is in EPSG:4326. Reproject first.
End cap style Flat stops a buffered line at its ends; Round (default) adds half circles.
Segments sets how smooth curves are; 5 is plenty for analysis.

Watch out

With Dissolve result and Keep disjoint results separate, every resulting piece keeps the fid of one input feature, so several pieces share a fid and saving to a GeoPackage fails with UNIQUE constraint failed. Run Renumber feature ids (Tool - QGIS) first.
A buffered polygon includes the original. For the zone around a shape only, see the fringe in the Proximity family.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Build virtual raster (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Build virtual raster (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Raster › Miscellaneous › Build Virtual Raster… (gdal:buildvirtualraster).
Realises:

Conversion and data management: stacking single-band rasters into one multiband layer, or joining tiles into one, without copying the data. The result is a small .vrt file that points to the inputs.

Settings that matter

Input layers: the bands, in the order they should have in the stack (band 1 first). Use the arrows in the selection dialog to order them.
Place each input file into a separate band: ticked to stack bands (B02, B03, B04, B08 → a four-band image); unticked to join tiles side by side.
Resolution: Highest keeps 10 m when 10 m and 20 m bands are mixed.

Watch out

The .vrt points to the input files: keep them in the same place, or the layer breaks.
In the stacked layer the bands are called Band 1, Band 2 … in input order. Write down which is which before styling a colour composite (Layer Properties › Symbology › Multiband color).

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Building heights from elevation models (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Building heights from elevation models (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › SemanticGIS › Raster analysis › Building heights from elevation models (DSM − DTM) (semanticgis:buildingheights, SemanticGIS plugin 0.7.19 and later).
Realises:

Building heights from elevation models (Task): map algebra (nDSM = DSM − DTM), an inward buffer and zonal statistics with an outlier filter, per building.

Settings that matter

Buildings (footprints): any polygon layer. Select the buildings of your study area and tick Selected features only.
Surface model (DSM) and Terrain model (DTM): leave both empty to use Danmarks Højdemodel (0.4 m), fetched for the buildings’ area only (needs your Datafordeleren key in the SemanticGIS panel). Or choose your own rasters, files or WCS layers, in the same CRS.
Advanced parameters (the defaults suit Danish town centres): resolution 0.4 m, inward buffer 0.5 m, percentile 95, outlier filter k = 3, eave percentile 10, flat roof below 1.0 m, at least 10 pixels.
Optional GeoTIFFs of the area: terrain (DTM, e.g. for Blender), surface (DSM) and height above ground (nDSM, to check the result).














































FieldMeaningheightTop of the building / ridge above ground (m): LOD1 extrusioneaveEstimated eave height above ground (m): LOD2 extrusionroof_riseheight − eave (m)roof_typeflat or pitchedgroundTerrain elevation under the building (m, DVR90)roof_absground + heighth_median, h_max_rawMedian and raw maximum height; a large h_max_raw shows how much was filteredn_pxPixels usedh_checkok, few pixels, no data, negative
Watch out

A lower wing inside the same footprint gives too low an eave and a large roof_rise: check those against the orthophoto.
“Few pixels” is usually a shed; “no data” a building outside the rasters.
The surface and terrain model must be from the same date: a building built between the two gets a nonsense height.
At most about 3 × 3 km of buildings per run at 0.4 m.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Clip (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Clip (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector overlay › Clip (native:clip); menu: Vector › Geoprocessing Tools › Clip.
Realises:

Clip
Clip to extent — with a rectangle (study area) as Overlay layer

Settings that matter

Only the input layer’s attributes are kept.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Clip project layers to GeoPackage (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Clip project layers to GeoPackage (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › SemanticGIS › Vector general › Clip project layers to one GeoPackage (semanticgis:cliptogeopackage, SemanticGIS plugin 0.7.19 and later).
Realises:

Clip of every visible layer by a study area, and Save of the results, with their styles, in one GeoPackage.

Settings that matter

Study area (polygon layer): everything is clipped to it; it is saved too.
Only visible layers: turn on the layers you want before running the tool.
Keep the layer styles: each clipped layer gets its source’s style as its default in the GeoPackage.
Also clip raster layers (to GeoTIFF): data rasters, also WCS layers such as Danmarks Højdemodel, are cut to the study area’s rectangle at their own resolution and saved in <name>_rasters next to the GeoPackage.
Add the clipped layers to the project: in a new group; switch the originals off and work with the copies.

Watch out

Map pictures (WMS, WMTS, XYZ basemaps) are not data and are skipped.
Layers keep their own CRS. Layer names become table names: Bygværk → bygvaerk.
An existing GeoPackage with the same name is replaced.
For Danish base data, Urban context for a study area fetches and clips in one step; use this tool for your own layers and for other countries.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Combination of values (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Combination of values (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › SemanticGIS › Vector table › Combination of values (unordered) (semanticgis:valuecombination, SemanticGIS plugin 0.7.18 and later).
Realises:

Derive a value per feature: the unordered set of the values a feature has in several fields, such as its crops through the years.

Settings that matter

Fields to combine: for a flattened series, the period columns (y2026_acr_class … y2021_acr_class).
Name of the new field: the combination is written as the distinct values, sorted and joined: Spring barley, Winter wheat whether barley came before wheat or after.
Add how often each value occurs: Spring barley ×2, Winter wheat ×4. Still unordered, but tells a wheat-dominated rotation from a barley-dominated one.
Count empty values as ‘(none)’: otherwise periods without a value are left out.
Add fields with the number of distinct values and of filled periods: …_n (1 = the same value every filled period) and …_periods (how many periods have a value). The log lists the ten most common combinations.

Watch out

Empty periods are left out, so a piece with a field in one year of six gets the same combination as a piece with that crop in all six. Filter on …_periods when the history must be complete.
Unordered means the sequence is gone. For questions where the order matters, such as nitrogen released when grass is ploughed, use the period columns themselves.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Count points in polygon (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Count points in polygon (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector analysis › Count points in polygon (native:countpointsinpolygon); menu: Vector › Analysis Tools › Count Points in Polygon.
Realises:

Summary by location — with count, or sum with a weight field

Settings that matter

Weight field: the field is summed instead of counting points.
Class field: counts the number of different values in each polygon, not how many points have each value.
Count field name: the name of the new field.

Watch out

It gives only one count or sum per run. For means, medians or several fields at once, use Join attributes by location (summary) (Tool - QGIS).

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Create grid (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Create grid (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector creation › Create grid (native:creategrid); menu: Vector › Research Tools › Create Grid.
Realises: generate grid — squares (Rectangle) or hexagons, or their points or lines.
Settings that matter

Grid type: Point, Line, Rectangle (Polygon), Diamond (Polygon) or Hexagon (Polygon).
Grid extent: from a layer or drawn on the map. Horizontal and Vertical spacing: the cell size, in the CRS’s units (metres in EPSG:25832).
Horizontal and Vertical overlay: overlap between cells; leave at 0 for a tiling grid.

Watch out

The grid starts at the extent’s corner. To line up with the Danish national square grid, start the extent at round kilometre values (e.g. 715000, 6170000) in EPSG:25832. The European statistical grid is in EPSG:3035 and starts at round kilometres there; it does not line up with the Danish grid.
A grid is a set of zones like any other: its cell size and origin are choices that change the result (the scale and zoning effects).

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Difference (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Difference (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector overlay › Difference (native:difference); menu: Vector › Geoprocessing Tools › Difference.
Realises:

Difference

Settings that matter

Input layer is A, Overlay layer is B: the result is A minus B.

Watch out

The order of the two layers matters. Read the help text in the dialog if unsure which is which.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Dissolve (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Dissolve (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector geometry › Dissolve (native:dissolve); menu: Vector › Geoprocessing Tools › Dissolve.
Realises:

Dissolve
Explode — with Keep disjoint features separate ticked

Settings that matter

Dissolve field(s) dissolves per value (one feature per category); leave it empty to dissolve everything.

Watch out

With Keep disjoint features separate the pieces can share a fid; see Renumber feature ids (Tool - QGIS).

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Download snapshot series (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Download snapshot series (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › SemanticGIS › Data access › Download snapshot series (WFS, one layer per year) (semanticgis:snapshotseries, SemanticGIS plugin 0.7.18 and later).
Realises:

Clip to extent and merge of a register published as one layer per year: every year of a period fetched for an area and written into one layer.

Settings that matter

Series: the registers the SemanticGIS catalogue knows as one WFS layer per year (Marker, Markblokke, Økologiske arealer, …). The list comes from the catalogue the SemanticGIS panel saves on your computer; open the panel once if the list is empty.
First year, Last year: the period. Years without a layer are skipped and named in the log.
Area and Buffer around the area (m): a polygon layer, or its selected features, and a margin.
Only features that touch the area: otherwise everything in the area’s bounding box is kept.
Clip features to the area: cut at the edge. Leave it off when you need whole fields, for example because an attribute gives the area of the whole field.
The output has the fields of all years (empty where a year lacks one), plus snapshot_year and snapshot_layer. The log lists the fields each year lacks and the attribution line; the line is also the output ATTRIBUTION.

Watch out

Fields differ between years: Marker has no crop before 2010, and other fields come and go (see the Marker note).
The tool asks the server only for the area’s bounding box. QGIS’s own WFS layer asks about the whole national layer first, which for Marker takes minutes.
A guard stops a year at 200,000 features; use a smaller area.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Extract by expression (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Extract by expression (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector selection › Extract by expression (native:extractbyexpression).
Realises:

Selection by attribute

Settings that matter

Expression in QGIS’s expression language: "hegnstype" = 'Levende', $area >= 50000 (m² in EPSG:25832).

Watch out

Text values are in single quotes, field names in double quotes.
Non-matching can be saved as a second output, useful to check what the condition left out.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Field calculator (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Field calculator (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector table › Field calculator (native:fieldcalculator); menu: Attribute table › Field calculator, or Processing Toolbox › Vector table.
Settings that matter

Result field type: Decimal (double), Integer (32 bit), Text …
Aggregate expressions summarise over groups: count($id, group_by:="cluster_id"), sum($area, group_by:="cluster_id").

Watch out

$area and $length are in the units of the layer’s CRS (or the project’s ellipsoid settings in the attribute table): check that they are m² and m.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Flatten snapshot series (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Flatten snapshot series (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › SemanticGIS › Vector overlay › Flatten snapshot series (newest geometry first) (semanticgis:flattensnapshots, SemanticGIS plugin 0.7.18 and later).
Realises:

Union of the periods of a layer, with snapping and sliver removal, so that each piece carries its value in every period: one column per field and period.

Settings that matter

Snapshot series: a polygon layer with several periods, for example the output of Download snapshot series. Join the fields you need first (names, classes); the tool does no joins.
Period field: the field that says which period a feature belongs to (snapshot_year).
Fields to keep: the fields to carry into the result, one column per period.
Tolerance: in the layer’s units, metres in a projected CRS. Older periods are snapped to the boundaries built so far within this distance, and pieces narrower than it are merged into the neighbour they share the longest boundary with.
Column prefix: put before the period in the column names: y gives y2026_acr_class; m for months, w for weeks. Periods are ordered by time, numbers and dates by value and text by the numbers in it.

Watch out

The newest period is kept as it is; older boundaries are moved onto it. If the newest period is the least accurate, the result inherits that.
Strips narrower than the tolerance are merged away even when they are real, such as a 2 m field margin with a 2 m tolerance. Choose the tolerance below the narrowest feature you care about.
Where an older feature’s outer edge snaps onto a newer boundary, the strip between them is no longer covered, so the result can cover slightly less than the input (0.1 % at Ledreborg).
The number of pieces can differ by a few between runs, because slivers can be merged in a different order. The areas do not change.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, November 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Graduated symbology (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Graduated symbology (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Layer Properties › Symbology, renderer Graduated. Not a Processing tool: it changes how a layer is drawn, not its data.
Realises:

Classification — through Mode: Equal Count (Quantile), Equal Interval, Fixed Interval, Logarithmic Scale, Natural Breaks (Jenks), Pretty Breaks, Standard Deviation
Classes shared between maps — with class boundaries edited by hand and the style saved and loaded on the other layers

Settings that matter

Value: a field or an expression (e.g. "samlet_areal_mean").
Mode and Classes: the method and number of classes. Classify recomputes the boundaries from the data.
Double-click a class’s Values to type its boundaries by hand; edit Legend to give classes readable labels.
Style › Save Style… writes a .qml file; Style › Load Style… on another layer applies the same classes and colours. Right-click a layer › Styles › Copy Style and Paste Style does the same between layers in a project.

Watch out

Every time you press Classify or change Mode, QGIS recomputes the boundaries from this layer’s values. Two layers classified separately get different boundaries, even with the same mode; for comparable maps, set the boundaries once and copy the style.
Features with an empty (NULL) value are not drawn at all. Show them, and areas with too few points, with a separate class: use Categorized or Rule-based on an expression, as in Comparable choropleth maps (Recipe - QGIS).

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Heatmap (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Heatmap (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Interpolation › Heatmap (Kernel Density Estimation) (qgis:heatmapkerneldensityestimation); Processing Toolbox only (also a renderer under Symbology › Heatmap, for display only).
Realises:

Kernel density

Settings that matter

Radius: in map units (metres in EPSG:25832). Output raster size: the cell size.
Kernel shape: Quartic, Triangular, Uniform, Triweight or Epanechnikov. Output value scaling: Raw or Scaled.
Weight from field: each point counts with the value of a field instead of 1.

Watch out

The Heatmap renderer in the layer’s symbology draws a density on screen but produces no data; the Processing tool makes a raster you can analyse.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Intersection (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Intersection (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector overlay › Intersection (native:intersection); menu: Vector › Geoprocessing Tools › Intersection.
Realises:

Intersection

Settings that matter

Overlay fields to keep limits which attributes of B are carried over.

Watch out

The result has the attributes of both layers. If you do not need B’s attributes, Clip (Tool - QGIS) gives the same shapes with a cleaner table.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Join attributes by field value (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Join attributes by field value (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector general › Join attributes by field value (native:joinattributestable). The same join can be made without a new layer under Layer Properties › Joins.
Realises: a join by key — the attributes of a second table added to each feature whose key field matches (the relational join of a database).
Settings that matter

Input layer and Table field: the layer that keeps its features (and geometry), and its key field.
Input layer 2 and Table field 2: the table whose fields are added, and its key field.
Layer 2 fields to copy: only the fields you need; empty copies all.
Join type: Create separate feature for each matching feature (one-to-many) or Take attributes of the first matching feature only (one-to-one).
Discard records which could not be joined, and the extra output Unjoinable features from first layer to see what did not match.
Joined field prefix: e.g. adr_, so fields with the same name in both tables stay apart.

Watch out

The output has the geometry of the Input layer. To put a table without geometry onto points, use the point layer as Input layer and the table as Input layer 2, with one-to-many when several rows share one point (several flats on one address point).
Both key fields must hold the same values in the same form: text "0101" does not match the number 101, and a UUID with capitals does not match one in lower case.
One-to-many multiplies features: count before and after the join.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Join attributes by location (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Join attributes by location (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector general › Join attributes by location (native:joinattributesbylocation); menu: Vector › Data Management Tools › Join Attributes by Location.
Realises:

Attribute transfer by location

Settings that matter

Features they (geometric predicate): the spatial relation, read as [Join to features in] [relation] [By comparing to]. Points first and zones second: “dwellings are within roder” (or intersect). See Spatial relations.
Join type: one-to-many, first matching feature only (one-to-one), or largest overlap only (one-to-one).

Watch out

One-to-many creates a copy of a feature for every match, so counts and areas can double. Use one-to-one unless you mean it.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.filePath: The technology stack/Processing Environments/QGIS/Tools/Join attributes by location (summary) (Tool - QGIS).md
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Join attributes by location (summary) (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector general › Join attributes by location (summary) (native:joinbylocationsummary); Processing Toolbox only.
Realises:

Summary by location

Settings that matter

Join to features in: the zones (they get the new fields). By comparing to: the points.
Where the features: the spatial relation, read as a sentence: [Join to features in] [relation] [By comparing to]. With zones first and points second, “roder contain boliger” is right; are within would ask whether a rode lies within a point, and every zone gets 0 without a warning. Ticking several boxes means or.

Points in zones: contain or intersect. A point exactly on a shared border is counted in both zones with intersect and in neither with contain; touch finds such points.
Polygons in zones (buildings, fields): intersect counts a polygon across a border in both zones, contain in neither.
All the relations, with tested examples: Spatial relations.


Fields to summarise: only the fields you need; empty means all fields.
Summaries to calculate: count, unique, min, max, range, sum, mean, median, stddev, minority, majority, q1, q3, iqr, … Output fields are named <field>_<summary>, e.g. samlet_areal_mean.
Discard records which could not be joined: leave unticked, or zones without points disappear from the map.

Watch out

The mean of a 0/1 indicator field is a share: summarise udlejet with mean to get the share rented.
Check that the counts add up to the number of points; points outside every zone are silently left out.

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.

the-technology-stack/processing-environm.title: Merge vector layers (Tool — QGIS)
the-technology-stack/processing-environm.content:
In QGIS: Processing Toolbox › Vector general › Merge vector layers (native:mergevectorlayers); menu: Vector › Data Management Tools › Merge Vector Layers.
Realises:

Merge

Settings that matter

Destination CRS reprojects layers that are in another system.
The output gets the fields layer and path, saying where each feature came from.

Watch out

All layers must have the same geometry type: buffer lines into polygons before merging them with polygons.
Fields with the same name but different types can make the merge fail; keep only the fields you need first (Retain fields).

Checked in QGIS 4.2.2, October 2026. Names and options can differ in other versions.
